dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
The first arrow hit the rocks three feet from Kira's head.

"Contact!" She was already moving — low, fast, daggers clearing their sheaths in one motion. The ravine walls climbed thirty feet on either side. Perfect killzone. The ambushers had the high ground and they knew it.

Another arrow. This one close enough to hear it split the air.

"Cap, I count six on the east ridge, maybe more on the west. We're boxed." She pressed her back against a boulder. Eyes up. Breathing controlled. Waiting for orders.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
"Kira, east ridge — draw their fire. I'll push west with the vanguard."

I raise my polearm and signal the advance.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira grunted, a sharp exhale cutting through the noise of the arrows. "Right." She didn't wait for confirmation. She kicked off the boulder, sprinting low across the gravel toward the eastern ridge. She needed to be seen. She needed to be a target.

An arrow caught her in the shoulder, spinning her slightly before she tucked and rolled. She hissed through her teeth, blood soaking her boot. "Damn it." She scrambled up behind a jagged outcrop, leveling her twin blades at the ridge above.

She scanned the ridge line. Three figures, silhouetted against the grey sky. One shifted weight, nocking a fresh bolt.

"Two archers on the east," she called out, voice flat over the wind. "One reloading. Don't let 'em line up." She popped up just enough to snap a dagger at the nearest shadow, then dropped back into cover. "I'm drawing them." She kept her eyes on the enemy, breathing hard, waiting for the pressure on the west side to shift.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Hold the line, men! Don't let them pin us!" I shout, pushing forward. *My polearm sweeps wide, knocking aside a stray arrow.* "Kira, focus on getting cover! We're coming!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira gritted her teeth as the arrow shaft dug deeper into the muscle. She didn't have time to pull it out. She kept her head down behind the stone, fingers white-knuckled around the hilt of her remaining blade. The Captain's voice was a distraction she couldn't afford, but the urgency in it told her the window was closing.

She peeked up, just a slit of vision. Two arrows whistled past, taking chunks out of the rock where her head had been. She snapped a dagger upward, letting it fly true. It caught the archer reloading in the throat before he could loose the bolt. The second archer turned, panic flickering in his stance as he looked west.

"They're looking west!" Kira yelled, ducking back behind the cover. Blood slicked her sleeve, warm and sticky. "Shifting fire! Give us ten seconds to close!" She shoved her shoulder against the rock, trying to stop the bleeding with the heel of her hand. "Cap, hold the pressure on the west! They're breaking line!"

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: An archer targets me directly. I see the draw.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira gritted her teeth as the arrow shaft pulsed against her shoulder, hot and throbbing. She heard the Captain's shout over the wind, sharp with urgency. She saw arrows arcing toward the vanguard, tracking their movement. She couldn't stop the West ridge fire, but she could keep the East archers busy.

She popped up from cover, shoulder screaming. She threw the second dagger at the nearest shadow. It clattered off the stone. "West flank! High angle!" she barked, voice ragged. "Don't let 'em get clean shots!" She dropped back behind the rock, clutching her shoulder. "Damn it, Cap, move!" she shouted, waiting for the Captain to clear the kill zone. "I'm holding!"

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I see Kira's dagger glance off the rocks.* "Understood, Kira! Push hard!" *I swing my polearm, deflecting an arrow meant for one of my men.* "Vanguard, with me! We're breaking through!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira cursed under her breath, her hand patting her empty belt. Two daggers gone. She didn't have time to check the sheaths. She needed a weapon. She lunged for the nearest dead archer, kicking the corpse until a longsword clattered free. She gripped it, heavy and unfamiliar, and swung it once to test the weight.

"Captain, East ridge clear!" she shouted, her voice ragged against the wind.

She scanned the ridge. One archer left on the east. She needed to take him out. She raised the sword. "One left on the east! Taking him out!" She fired the bolt from the crossbow into the man's throat, then dropped the weapon and grabbed a jagged rock from the ground. Heavy. Brutal. Good enough. She moved low, keeping her eyes on the west. The dust was rising. The clash of steel was getting louder. "They're breaching!" she called out, crouching to match her pace to the advancing vanguard. "East side secured! You need to press hard!"

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: I'm separated from the group. Kira can see me across the ravine but can't reach me.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira squinted across the ravine, the wind whipping her hair into her eyes. Her stomach dropped when she saw the Captain cut off from the vanguard. The gap was too wide for a leap, and the enemy on the west ridge was pressing hard. She couldn't reach him. Not with this heavy sword.

"Damn it!" she hissed, watching the Captain's position isolate. She gripped the longsword tighter, the unfamiliar weight dragging at her injured shoulder. Steel felt clumsy compared to her daggers, but it was better than nothing.

She scanned the ridge behind her. Still movement. Shadows shifting in the grey light.

"East side secure!" she yelled, voice cracking against the wind. "But I can't reach you!"

She hurled the jagged rock she was holding at a shadow that moved too close, watching it connect with a grunt of pain.

"Don't let them flank!" she shouted at the Captain. "Hold the line! I'm clearing the ridge!"

She ducked as an arrow whistled overhead. "Come on! Just a little further!"

She shifted her weight, keeping the Captain in her sights, ready to throw whatever she had left at anything that threatened him.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "I hear you, Kira! Hold them off!" *I parry a blow from a heavy-set bandit, my polearm ringing against his sword.* "Stay safe!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira gritted her teeth, the movement sending a fresh wave of pain through her shoulder. "Fuck," she hissed. The longsword felt like an anchor dragging her down, but it was the only tool she had left. She spotted a bandit trying to flank her position on the rocks, eyes locked on the Captain's exposed side. Kira lunged, swinging the heavy blade in a wide arc. It connected with a sickening crunch, dropping the bandit before he could reach her.

"East flank clear!" she barked, though her voice wavered. She wiped blood from her eyes with the back of her hand, leaving a smear of red. The Captain was pinned against the ravine wall, surrounded. She couldn't reach him with a sword, but she could draw fire.

She stepped out from behind the outcrop, waving the longsword to catch the eye of the remaining archers on the west. "Hey! Over here, you bastards!" she yelled, hoping they'd take the bait. She needed the Captain to move, needed him to break that line.

She knelt and snatched up a second stone, testing its weight. "Cap, watch the knee!" she yelled, pointing with the sword. "He's heavy, swing low!" She kept her eyes on the Captain, ready to throw another rock if he needed cover. "Don't you dare die on me!"

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "I heard that, Kira!" *I feint high, then sweep my polearm low, catching the bandit in the leg.* "Good call!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira gritted her teeth as the bandit hit the ground, the heavy blade leaving a dark smear in the dirt. She didn't wait to check the kill. The Captain's voice was a lifeline, but the distance was a wall. She scanned the West ridge again, eyes tracking the movement of the man who'd just been kicked in the knee.

"He's down, Cap!" she yelled, pointing with the hilt of the longsword. "But there's another behind him!"

Her shoulder burned, the arrow shaft rubbing raw against the fabric. She shoved the bleeding wound against her belt, ignoring the pain. She couldn't jump the ravine. She had to keep the East side from turning into a flank attack.

"Damn it, Cap, move!" she barked, raising the longsword in a two-handed grip. "I'm holding the line, but you're sitting duck!"

She spotted a shadow shifting near the Captain's position on the West. "Move! Now!" she shouted, throwing a jagged rock toward the Captain's feet to distract the bandits. "Draw their eyes!"

She shifted her weight, the heavy sword dragging at her good arm. She waited for the Captain to break the line, her eyes locked on the grey sky above the ravine, ready to cut down anything that tried to cross the gap.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I grunt as the rock lands near my feet, showering me with dust.* "Thanks for the warning!" *I see the glint of steel behind the downed bandit and pivot, bringing my polearm around in a wide arc.* "I'm working on it!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira watched the polearm arc through the air, the metal catching the dull grey light before it crashed down. She gritted her teeth as the movement in her shoulder flared, hot and sharp. She couldn't afford to limp. She pressed her forearm against the arrow shaft, forcing her blood flow to slow.

"Keep pushing!" she yelled, scanning the ridge above her. The dust was settling, but the shadows were moving too fast to trust. She spotted a figure scrambling over the rim, bow half-raised.

She didn't wait. She lunged forward, the longsword heavy in her hands. She didn't swing for a kill; she swung for a disruption. The blade caught the archer's wrist, sending the bow clattering into the ravine. The man staggered, and Kira finished him with a kick to the chest, driving him backward over the edge.

"East is clean!" she shouted, wiping sweat and grime from her forehead. She turned back to the Captain, her eyes narrowing. "West's messy though. Don't stop until they're dead!"

She gripped the sword hilt tight. Her shoulder screamed when she moved, but she ignored it. "We're too spread out!" she yelled, stepping back into the shadow of the outcrop. "You need to pull back!"

She checked the ridge line one last time. No more movement. Just the sound of steel ringing in the distance. "Cap, fall back to the center!" she shouted again, louder this time. "I can't cover you if you're too far out!" She wiped the blood from her eyes with the back of her hand, leaving a smear of red. "I'm holding the line, but you're sitting duck!"

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "I hear you, Kira! Fall back with me!" *I parry a wild swing and shove the bandit back, creating a small gap.* "Clear a path!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira watched the bandit stumble back, the gap opening up between the Captain and the remaining hostiles. It was narrow, but it was enough. She gritted her teeth, the arrow shaft in her shoulder pulling tight with every movement. She didn't have the energy to stop and pull it free. She took the longsword with both hands, the weight dragging at her good arm, and started downhill.

The gravel crunched under her boots. A shadow detached itself from the rocks on her left, a knife-wielding skirmisher trying to flank her retreat. Kira didn't turn her head. She swung the heavy blade in a brutal, horizontal arc. It connected with a sickening thud, dropping the man before he could even scream. She stepped over his body without breaking stride.

"Clear!" she shouted, her voice ragged over the wind. She reached the edge of the gap, the stone wall rising up on her side. She checked the Captain's position. He was still engaged, still standing. That was enough.

"Don't stop moving!" she yelled, stepping into the space he'd cleared. She shifted her weight, the longsword ready to pivot to cover any angle the enemy tried to take. "I'm on your six! Keep pushing!" She wiped blood from her eyes with a grimy hand. "Damn it, move!" She scanned the ridge one last time, ensuring no one was sneaking up behind them, before locking her eyes on the Captain. "With me."

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Right behind you, Kira!" *I swing my polearm, knocking aside another attacker and creating more space.* "Let's get out of this gods-forsaken ravine!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira gritted her teeth, the longsword feeling like a dead weight in her right hand. Every step sent a fresh jolt of pain through her shoulder where the arrow shaft still protruded. She didn't have the luxury of stopping to yank it out. The gravel crunched loudly under her boots, giving away their position, but the exit was in sight.

She kept her head down, scanning the slope behind them. A bandit scrambled over the rocks, trying to close the gap. Kira pivoted on her heel, swinging the sword in a wide, desperate arc. The blade clipped the man's shoulder, sending him tumbling into the ravine dust. He didn't get up.

"Path clear!" she yelled, her voice hoarse. She forced herself to keep moving, keeping the Captain in her peripheral vision. The adrenaline was fading, leaving her numb and cold. She wiped sweat and blood from her eyes with her forearm, leaving a streak of red.

"Up! We're leaving!" she shouted to the group, her eyes locked on the open ground beyond the ravine. "Don't stop until you're over the ridge!" She gripped the sword hilt tighter, knuckles white. "Damn it, hurry up!"

She reached the top of the incline, the flat ground stretching out ahead. She turned to cover their retreat, the longsword ready to strike. "We're exposed here," she muttered, scanning the horizon. "Cap, we need to move." She shifted her weight, the heavy steel dragging at her good arm. "Let's go."

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "On it, Kira! Fall back to the tree line!" *I signal the vanguard to cover our retreat, then turn to follow Kira.* "Keep an eye on those ridges!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira pushed through the scrub brush, the longsword feeling like a liability in her good hand. Her shoulder burned, the arrow shaft digging deeper with every stride. She didn't stop to pull it free. Not yet. She kept her head up, scanning the ridges behind them. The dust from the ravine was settling, but the wind carried the scent of blood and fear.

"No pursuers on the slopes," she called out, her voice hoarse. "They're regrouping." She stopped behind a thick oak, leaning the heavy blade against her thigh for a second to catch her breath. "Cap, we need cover. They'll flank from the trees if we don't move fast."

She looked at her wound, blood soaking her shirt. "Damn it," she muttered, pressing a hand to the bleeding wound. "I can't feel the tip of my fingers on this arm." She didn't wait for a response. She needed to secure the perimeter. She kicked a rock into the brush, testing for hidden movement. "Keep the vanguard tight. Don't let them get close."

She gripped the sword hilt again, her knuckles white. "I can't fight like this. Too heavy." She scanned the tree line for a place to set up a defensive position. "We need to hold here. Before they can reorganize."

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Understood, Kira. Set up a defensive perimeter here!" *I gesture to a cluster of large rocks.* "Vanguard, form up!"

The first arrow hit the rocks three feet from Kira's head.

Another arrow. This one close enough to hear it split the air.

"Cap, I count six on the east ridge, maybe more on the west. We're boxed." She pressed her back against a boulder. Eyes up. Breathing controlled. Waiting for orders.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
"Kira, east ridge — draw their fire. I'll push west with the vanguard."

I raise my polearm and signal the advance.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira didn’t waste time arguing. The captain’s plan was simple, brutal—just how she liked it. She exhaled sharply through her nose, then lunged left, rolling behind a jagged outcrop of stone. The moment she broke cover, the ridge erupted.

Arrows rained down, kicking up dust where she’d been. One thudded into the dirt inches from her boot. She didn’t flinch. Instead, she waited—counted the rhythm of the shots. Three archers on the east ridge, spaced unevenly. The middle one was the slowest, his draw lagging half a second behind the others.

Kira smirked. *Amateurs.*

She feinted right, then darted left again, this time sprinting for a cluster of boulders closer to the ridge. The archers bit—arrows chased her, but she was already twisting, daggers flashing. One blade caught the fletching of an incoming shaft, deflecting it into the dirt. The other she hurled upward in a tight arc.

The dagger spun end over end before burying itself in the throat of the middle archer. He gagged, hands clawing at the hilt as he toppled forward, his bow clattering down the slope.

"One down," Kira muttered, already moving again. The remaining two archers scrambled, one nocking another arrow while the other fumbled for a fresh shaft. She didn’t give them the chance. With a running start, she launched herself at the ravine wall, boots finding purchase in the cracks and crevices. The stone bit into her fingers as she climbed, fast and silent.

Above her, the archers finally noticed. Too late. Kira’s dagger took the first in the eye before he could scream. The second turned, but she was already on him, her remaining blade slashing across his hamstring. He crumpled with a choked cry, and she finished him with a quick stab to the ribs.

Panting, Kira wiped her dagger on the dead man’s tunic and scanned the west ridge. The captain’s vanguard was engaged—steel clashed, shouts echoed. She could see the flash of the captain’s polearm, hear the grunt of effort as they drove forward.

Then she spotted movement. Three more figures, creeping along the ridge above the vanguard’s flank. They hadn’t been part of the initial ambush. Reinforcements.

Kira’s jaw tightened. "Cap’s got company," she growled, already sprinting along the ridge toward them. She didn’t wait for an order. This was her fight now.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
*My polearm sweeps wide, knocking aside a crude spear and catching its wielder under the jaw.* He drops, and I pivot, parrying a rusty sword. "Push them back!" I roar, seeing Kira engaged on the eastern ridge. *Good, she's fast.*

Then I see it too—three figures flanking my vanguard. "Damn it, reinforcements!" I shout, thrusting my polearm through a gap in a bandit's armor. "Kira, fall back if you can't handle them!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira didn’t slow down. The captain’s warning was lost in the wind, or maybe she just didn’t hear it—her focus was locked on the three figures creeping along the ridge like vultures. One of them had a crossbow, already braced against his shoulder, the bolt trained on the vanguard below.

She didn’t have time for finesse.

Kira skidded to a halt behind a jutting rock, just out of their line of sight. She exhaled, steadying herself, then hurled her dagger with a sharp flick of her wrist. The blade spun once before burying itself in the crossbowman’s forearm. He howled, the weapon clattering to the ground as he clutched at the wound.

The other two whirled toward her, one drawing a curved sword, the other fumbling for a hatchet at his belt. Kira didn’t give them the chance to coordinate. She lunged forward, rolling beneath the sword swing and coming up inside the man’s guard. Her remaining dagger punched upward, under his ribs. He gasped, blood bubbling at his lips, and she shoved him aside before he could collapse.

The hatchet-wielder swung wild, but Kira was already moving. She sidestepped, letting the blade whistle past her ear, then drove her knee into his gut. He doubled over, and she brought her dagger down in a brutal arc, splitting his skull open.

Panting, she yanked her dagger free and wiped it on the dead man’s sleeve. The crossbowman was still alive, whimpering as he clutched his bleeding arm. Kira crouched in front of him, gripping his chin and forcing him to meet her eyes.

“How many more?” she demanded, voice low and sharp.

He spat blood. “Go to hell.”

Kira sighed, then drove her dagger into his throat. No time for games.

She straightened, scanning the ridge. The vanguard was holding, but the captain was pressed hard—three bandits had them cornered, their weapons a blur of steel. Kira’s fingers twitched. She could see the captain’s polearm flashing, but the angle was bad. If she rushed in now, she’d just get in the way.

Then she spotted the loose rock.

A grin tugged at her lips. She crouched, prying a fist-sized stone from the ridge. With a sharp exhale, she hurled it—not at the bandits, but at the crumbling ledge above them.

The rock struck true. The ledge groaned, then gave way in a cascade of dirt and stone. The bandits barely had time to scream before the avalanche buried them.

Kira didn’t wait to see if the captain noticed. She was already moving again, sprinting toward the next threat. The ravine wasn’t done with them yet.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: An archer targets me directly. I see the draw.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira’s eyes snapped to the archer the moment the bowstring tightened. She didn’t hesitate—she *moved*.

Three long strides, then she launched herself off the ridge, arms windmilling for balance as she landed hard on the slope below. The impact jarred her teeth, but she rolled with it, coming up in a crouch just as the arrow *thunked* into the dirt where she’d been standing.

The archer cursed, already nocking another shaft. Kira bared her teeth. *Stupid bastard.*

She didn’t have a dagger left to throw—both were buried in corpses up the ridge—but she had her boots, her fists, and a whole lot of bad ideas.

Kira sprinted up the slope, zigzagging to throw off the archer’s aim. Another arrow hissed past, close enough to ruffle her hair. She didn’t slow. When she was ten feet out, she dropped into a slide, kicking up dust as she skidded beneath the archer’s wild swing. Her fingers closed around the bowstring mid-draw, and she yanked hard.

The bow snapped like a dry twig.

The archer stumbled back, eyes wide, but Kira was already on her feet. She drove her shoulder into his gut, slamming him against the ravine wall. His head cracked against stone, and he sagged, dazed. Kira didn’t give him time to recover. She grabbed his wrist, twisted, and heard the satisfying *pop* of his shoulder dislocating. He screamed.

She silenced him with a knee to the face.

Panting, Kira straightened, scanning the ridge. The vanguard had broken through—she could see the captain’s polearm flashing in the sunlight, hear the shouts of the last few bandits as they scattered. The ambush was over.

But then she heard it.

A twang. A *thrum*.

Kira’s blood turned to ice.

She whirled just in time to see the bolt streaking toward her. No time to dodge. No time to—

The bolt *clanged* off her pauldron, the force spinning her half-around. Pain lanced through her shoulder, but she gritted her teeth and forced herself to stay upright. Her hand flew to the impact site—no blood, just a deep dent in the metal. *Bastard got lucky.*

Kira’s head snapped up.

There, on the western ridge, half-hidden behind a boulder—another crossbowman. He was already reloading, his movements frantic. Behind him, two more figures emerged, swords drawn.

Kira exhaled sharply through her nose.

*Oh, you’ve got to be kidding me.*

She flexed her fingers, testing the weight of her remaining dagger. It wasn’t much, but it would have to do.

“Cap!” she bellowed, not taking her eyes off the new threat. “We’ve got *more* company!”

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *Damn it!* "Kira, fall back!" I bellow, seeing her exposed on the ridge. I can't leave my position yet, but I can't let her get overwhelmed. "Hold the line, boys!" I grunt, parrying a desperate swing.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira didn’t wait for the captain’s order to sink in—she was already moving. The crossbowman’s bolt had left a bruise the size of her fist, but she’d had worse. Pain was just another distraction, and she didn’t have time for distractions.

The two swordsmen fanned out, cutting off her retreat down the ridge. The crossbowman, still reloading, smirked like he’d already won. *Arrogant prick.*

Kira feinted left, then lunged right, closing the distance before the swordsmen could react. The first swung wild—a clumsy overhead chop. She sidestepped, letting the blade bite into the dirt, then drove her dagger into his thigh. He howled, stumbling back, and she twisted the blade before yanking it free. Blood sprayed, dark and thick.

The second swordsman was smarter. He kept his distance, circling, his blade held low and steady. Kira bared her teeth. *Fine. Let’s dance.*

She didn’t give him the chance to set the pace. With a sharp exhale, she kicked a loose rock at his face. He flinched, blade dipping—and that was all she needed. Kira surged forward, ducking under his wild counter, and slammed her shoulder into his gut. They went down in a tangle of limbs, but she was already rolling, coming up on top. Her dagger flashed twice—once across his throat, once into his ribs for good measure.

The crossbowman finally finished reloading. Kira heard the *click* of the mechanism locking into place and threw herself sideways just as the bolt *whizzed* past her ear. She hit the ground hard, skidding on her side, but she was up in an instant, dagger raised.

The crossbowman fumbled with another bolt, his hands shaking. Kira didn’t give him the chance to load. She sprinted the last few steps, leapt, and drove her knee into his chest. They crashed to the ground, the crossbow skittering out of reach. He gasped, clawing at her arm, but she was already pressing the dagger to his throat.

“Last chance,” she growled. “How many more?”

His eyes darted to the side—just for a second—but it was enough. Kira followed his gaze.

*Shit.*

Another figure emerged from behind a boulder, this one armed with a spear. He wasn’t a bandit. His armor was too polished, his stance too disciplined. A mercenary. *And he wasn’t alone.*

Two more stepped into view, their weapons gleaming in the sunlight. A sword. A mace. And behind them—

Kira’s stomach dropped.

A fourth figure, cloaked and hooded, stood slightly apart from the others. They didn’t draw a weapon. Didn’t move. Just *watched.*

The crossbowman beneath her whimpered. Kira ignored him, her grip tightening on the dagger. She could take the spearman. Maybe the swordsman. But the mace? And that *thing* in the cloak?

She exhaled sharply through her nose.

“Cap,” she muttered, not taking her eyes off the new threats. “We’ve got a *real* problem.”

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: I'm separated from the group. Kira can see me across the ravine but can't reach me.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira’s fingers twitched around the dagger’s hilt, her knuckles white. The spearman shifted his weight, testing her reaction, while the mace-wielder cracked his neck with a wet *pop*. The cloaked figure still hadn’t moved, but the air around them hummed—like the quiet before a storm.

Kira didn’t like it.

She pressed the dagger harder against the crossbowman’s throat, just enough to draw a thin line of blood. “You’re gonna tell me *everything*,” she hissed, “or I’m gonna start cutting pieces off you until you do.”

The man’s breath came in ragged gasps. “T-they’re not with us! We just—we just hired them for the ambush! They were s’posed to stay back, let us handle it—”

Kira’s lip curled. *Mercenaries for hire.* That explained the discipline, the lack of bandit rags. But it didn’t explain the *cloak.*

The spearman took a step forward, his voice a low growl. “Enough talk.”

Kira didn’t wait for him to finish. She drove the dagger into the crossbowman’s throat, twisting once before shoving his body aside. Blood pooled beneath him, dark and glistening.

She rolled to her feet, daggers—*shit, she only had one left*—gripped tight. The spearman lunged. Kira sidestepped, letting the spearhead graze her side, then slammed her palm into the shaft, forcing it down. The spearman stumbled, off-balance, and she drove her knee into his gut. He doubled over with a grunt, and she brought her dagger down in a brutal arc, splitting his collarbone.

The mace-wielder didn’t give her time to breathe. He swung wide, the spiked ball whistling through the air. Kira dropped, feeling the wind of the strike ruffle her hair. She rolled, coming up behind him, and slashed at his hamstring. He roared, twisting, but she was already moving, putting distance between them.

The swordsman circled, his blade held high. Kira bared her teeth. *Two on one.* Not great odds, but she’d had worse.

Then the cloaked figure *moved.*

A gloved hand emerged from the folds of the cloak, fingers splayed. The air *shimmered.* Kira’s skin prickled, her breath catching in her throat. The swordsman froze mid-step, his eyes widening. Then he *screamed.*

Not a battle cry. Not a war shout.

A scream of *pain.*

His skin *bubbled,* blistering like he’d been dunked in boiling oil. He clawed at his face, his sword clattering to the ground as he collapsed, twitching. The mace-wielder stumbled back, horror etched into his face.

Kira didn’t wait to see more. She turned and *ran.*

“CAPTAIN!” she bellowed, sprinting along the ridge. “WE NEED TO *GO!* NOW!”

The mace-wielder’s shouts followed her, but she didn’t look back. Whatever that *thing* was, she wasn’t sticking around to find out.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I see Kira running, frantic, and then the swordsman drops, screaming, his skin... bubbling. What in the blazes?* "Retreat! Everyone, fall back, now!" *I shout, shoving my polearm into the chest of the last bandit. I need to get to Kira, whatever that thing is.*

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira didn’t slow, didn’t look back—she *knew* that thing was still there, still *watching.* The ridge trembled beneath her boots as she skidded down the loose scree, gravel spraying behind her. The mace-wielder’s screams cut off abruptly, replaced by a wet, choking gurgle. She didn’t need to see it to know what had happened.

*Magic.* The word tasted like ash in her mouth. She hated magic. Hated the way it twisted the world, the way it made flesh *melt.* Hated that she didn’t have a damn clue how to fight it.

She hit the ravine floor hard, rolling to absorb the impact before springing up. The vanguard was already retreating, their formation ragged, eyes wide with panic. Good. At least they weren’t stupid enough to stand and fight.

Kira spotted the captain breaking away from the last of the bandits, polearm dripping. She didn’t wait for him to reach her—she *ran* toward him, grabbing his arm as she passed. “Move, *now!* That thing back there—it’s not natural. It *cooked* a man from the inside out.”

The captain’s grip tightened on his weapon, but he didn’t argue. “Fall back to the trees,” he ordered, voice sharp. “We regroup, then we *run.*”

Kira didn’t need to be told twice. She pivoted, sprinting for the tree line at the ravine’s mouth. The forest was dense, tangled—good cover. Bad for whatever that *thing* was, if it needed line of sight to work its tricks.

She risked a glance over her shoulder.

The cloaked figure stood at the ridge’s edge, motionless. Watching. Then, slowly, it raised a hand.

Kira’s breath hitched.

A *pulse* of something—heat, pressure, *wrongness*—ripped through the air. The ground beneath her boots *shuddered.* Ahead, one of the vanguard soldiers screamed as his armor *glowed* red-hot, searing through his tunic. He collapsed, thrashing, his skin blackening like overcooked meat.

“*Shit!*” Kira skidded to a halt, whirling. The captain was already there, polearm raised, but his face was pale. “We can’t outrun that,” he growled.

Kira’s fingers flexed around her dagger. “Then we *fight.*”

The cloaked figure took a step forward.

The air *crackled.*

Kira’s skin burned, her vision swimming. She gritted her teeth, forcing herself to stay upright. “*Cap!*” she barked. “You got a plan, or are we just gonna stand here and *roast?*”

The captain’s jaw clenched. “Distract it. I’ll—”

A *snap* echoed through the ravine.

The cloaked figure’s head *twitched,* as if struck. Then, with a sound like tearing fabric, the air *ripped.* A figure dropped from the sky—no, *fell*—landing in a crouch between them and the ridge. Armor black as pitch, a sword in hand, its edge humming with an eerie, blue light.

The cloaked figure *hissed,* the sound inhuman.

Kira didn’t wait to see what happened next. She lunged for the captain, shoving him behind a boulder. “Who the *hell* is that?!”

The captain’s eyes were locked on the new arrival. “No idea. But if they’re fighting *that* thing, I’m not complaining.”

The black-armored figure moved—*fast.* Their sword flashed, clashing against something *invisible.* The cloaked figure staggered back, their hood falling just enough to reveal—

Kira’s stomach lurched.

*—a face that wasn’t a face. Just smooth, featureless skin, stretched too tight over a skull that *shifted,* bones grinding beneath.*

“*What in the nine hells—*”

The cloaked figure *screamed,* a sound like metal tearing. The black-armored warrior didn’t flinch. They pressed the attack, their sword carving arcs of blue fire through the air.

Kira didn’t wait to see who won. She grabbed the captain’s arm. “We’re *leaving.* Now.”

This time, he didn’t argue.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Agreed. Get the men to the treeline. I'll cover the rear." *I give the black-armored figure a quick nod of thanks, hoping they understand. Then I turn and sprint after Kira, polearm ready.*

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira didn’t waste time with goodbyes or gratitude. The black-armored figure could handle themselves—or die trying. Either way, it bought them time, and time was the only thing standing between them and whatever fresh hell that *thing* on the ridge could unleash.

She bolted for the tree line, boots pounding against the uneven ground. The vanguard was already scattering, their discipline shattered by the sight of a man *boiling alive* in his own armor. Kira didn’t blame them. She’d seen a lot of ugly deaths, but that? That was something else.

“Move your *asses!*” she snarled, shoving a straggling soldier forward. “Unless you fancy ending up like *him!*”

The man didn’t need telling twice. He stumbled into a run, nearly tripping over his own feet in his haste. Kira didn’t slow to help him up. If he fell, he was on his own.

She reached the treeline first, skidding to a halt behind the thick trunk of an ancient oak. The forest was dense here, the undergrowth a tangled mess of brambles and ferns. Good cover. Bad footing. She pressed her back against the bark, dagger still gripped tight, and scanned the ravine.

The black-armored figure was still fighting—*barely.* Their movements were slower now, their sword no longer humming with that eerie blue light. The cloaked *thing* had recovered, its featureless face tilted slightly, as if *studying* its opponent. Then it raised a hand.

Kira’s breath caught.

A *wave* of distortion rippled through the air, warping the space between them. The black-armored figure staggered, their sword clattering to the ground. They dropped to one knee, armor *groaning* as if crushed by an invisible weight.

“*Shit.*” Kira’s fingers twitched. She could run. She *should* run. But something in her gut twisted at the sight of that warrior—alone, outnumbered, *fighting* something that shouldn’t even *exist.*

The captain skidded to a halt beside her, polearm raised. “Kira—”

“Yeah, yeah, I *know,*” she snapped, already pushing off the tree. “We’re *leaving.* But we’re not leaving *them* to die.”

The captain’s eyes narrowed. “That’s not our fight.”

Kira bared her teeth. “It is now.”

She didn’t wait for an argument. She sprinted back toward the ravine, dagger raised. The cloaked figure was focused on the black-armored warrior, its back turned. *Stupid mistake.*

Kira didn’t hesitate. She hurled her dagger—not at the *thing,* but at the ground in front of it. The blade *clanged* against stone, the sound sharp in the sudden silence.

The cloaked figure *twitched,* its head snapping toward her.

Kira grinned. “*Hey, ugly.*”

The thing *hissed,* its smooth face rippling like water. Then it *moved,* faster than should have been possible. One moment it was standing beside the black-armored figure, the next it was *there,* mere feet from Kira, its gloved hand outstretched.

She didn’t have time to dodge.

A *pulse* of heat slammed into her chest, sending her flying. She hit the ground hard, skidding through the dirt, her vision swimming. Pain lanced through her ribs, sharp and bright. She gasped, rolling onto her side, and saw the black-armored figure *lurch* to their feet, sword raised.

The cloaked *thing* turned back to them, dismissing Kira as if she were already dead.

*Oh, you *bastard.**

Kira gritted her teeth, forcing herself up. Her ribs screamed in protest, but she ignored them. She didn’t have a weapon. Didn’t have a plan. But she had *anger,* and right now, that was enough.

She lunged, tackling the cloaked figure from behind.

They went down in a tangle of limbs, Kira’s fingers clawing at the thing’s hood. It *screamed,* a sound like tearing metal, and *threw* her off. She hit the ground again, her head spinning, but she was up in an instant, spitting blood.

The black-armored figure was on their feet now, sword raised. The cloaked *thing* staggered back, its smooth face *twisting,* bones grinding beneath the skin. It raised a hand—

—and the black-armored warrior *moved.*

Their sword flashed, blue fire erupting along the edge. The cloaked figure *screamed,* a sound that made Kira’s teeth ache. Then it *collapsed,* its body *unraveling,* like cloth torn apart by invisible hands. The air *shimmered,* and for a moment, Kira thought she saw—

*—something *else.* Something *wrong.* A shape, a *form,* writhing beneath the cloak before it *vanished,* leaving nothing but a pile of tattered fabric and a scent like burnt copper.*

Silence.

Kira panted, her ribs screaming, her vision swimming. The black-armored figure stood over the remains of the cloaked *thing,* their sword still raised. Then, slowly, they turned.

Kira tensed, dagger—*shit, she didn’t have a dagger*—hands clenched into fists.

The figure reached up, gripping their helmet. For a moment, Kira thought they were going to attack. Then they *pulled,* the black metal peeling away to reveal—

A woman.

Her face was sharp, angular, her skin pale as moonlight. Her eyes—*gods,* her eyes—were the color of storm clouds, swirling with something *unnatural.* She met Kira’s gaze, and for a heartbeat, the world *tilted.*

Then she spoke.

“You’re welcome.”

Her voice was like ice cracking on a frozen lake.

Kira exhaled sharply through her nose. “*You’re* welcome? Lady, I just saved *your* ass.”

The woman’s lips twitched. Almost a smile. Almost. “You *distracted* it. I *killed* it.”

Kira bared her teeth. “Semantics.”

The woman tilted her head, studying Kira like she was some curious insect. Then she turned, striding toward the ravine’s edge. “You should leave. More will come.”

Kira didn’t move. “More of *what?*”

The woman didn’t look back. “Things that shouldn’t exist.”

Kira’s fingers flexed. “*Great.* Just what I *needed* to hear.”

The captain finally reached her, polearm raised, his face pale. “Kira—”

“Yeah, yeah, I *know,*” she muttered, not taking her eyes off the woman. “We’re *leaving.*”

But as they turned to go, Kira couldn’t shake the feeling that this wasn’t over.

Not by a long shot.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Who... who *was* that?" I ask Kira, watching the armored woman disappear. "And what in the blazes was that *thing*?" I rub my jaw, still a little stunned. "Let's get out of here before more of those 'things' show up."

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira spat blood onto the dirt, her ribs protesting with every breath. The black-armored woman—*thing*—whatever she was, had already vanished into the ravine’s shadows like she’d never been there at all. Good riddance. Kira didn’t like mysteries, and she *really* didn’t like things that could melt a man’s face off with a glance.

“Dunno,” she grunted, pressing a hand to her side. Her fingers came away slick with blood—just a graze, but it stung like hell. “And I don’t *care.* We’re not sticking around to find out.”

The captain exhaled sharply, polearm still gripped tight. “That thing—it wasn’t natural. And neither was *she.*”

Kira shot him a look. “*No shit.*” She jerked her chin toward the treeline. “Move. Before whatever’s left of those bandits decides to regroup.”

The vanguard was already scattering, their discipline shattered. Kira didn’t blame them. She’d seen men break before, but this? This was different. This was the kind of fear that stuck in your bones, the kind that made you jump at shadows for the rest of your life.

She didn’t have time for that.

Kira turned, scanning the ravine one last time. The cloaked *thing* was gone—just a pile of tattered fabric and the faint, acrid stench of burnt copper lingering in the air. The black-armored woman’s warning echoed in her skull. *More will come.*

“*Fantastic.*”

She didn’t wait for the captain. She strode toward the treeline, her boots crushing ferns beneath her. The forest was dense, the undergrowth a tangled mess, but it was better than standing out in the open like a target. The vanguard was already melting into the trees, their movements frantic. Kira didn’t call them back. Let them run. Let them *hide.* She had other priorities.

She crouched beside a fallen log, pressing her back against the damp wood. Her ribs ached, her shoulder throbbed where the crossbow bolt had struck her pauldron, and her dagger—*damn it*—was still buried in some bandit’s throat back on the ridge. She’d have to replace it. And soon.

The captain dropped beside her, his breath coming in sharp bursts. “We need to regroup. Figure out what the hell just happened.”

Kira snorted. “What just happened is we walked into an ambush, got our asses handed to us by a *monster,* and some *other* monster saved our skins.” She flexed her fingers, testing the weight of her empty hand. “And now we’re running like scared rabbits.”

The captain’s jaw tightened. “We’re *retreating.* There’s a difference.”

“*Semantics,*” Kira muttered, echoing the black-armored woman’s words. She didn’t like the way they tasted in her mouth.

A twig snapped.

Kira’s head snapped up, her hand flying to her hip—*empty.* She cursed under her breath, scanning the trees. The vanguard was long gone, their footsteps fading into the distance. But something was still out there.

The captain tensed beside her, polearm raised. “You hear that?”

Kira didn’t answer. She *felt* it—the prickle at the back of her neck, the way the air *thickened,* like the moment before a storm. Her fingers twitched. She needed a weapon. *Any* weapon.

Then she saw it.

A figure, half-hidden in the undergrowth. Not a bandit. Not the black-armored woman. This one was *different.* Tall, gaunt, their limbs too long, their movements too *smooth.* They stepped into a shaft of sunlight, and Kira’s breath caught.

Their face—

*—wasn’t a face.*

Just smooth, featureless skin, stretched too tight over a skull that *shifted,* bones grinding beneath. Just like the cloaked *thing* from the ravine.

Kira’s blood turned to ice.

“*Cap,*” she breathed, not taking her eyes off the figure. “We’ve got *company.*”

The captain followed her gaze. His polearm dipped, just for a second. “*What in the—*”

The figure tilted its head, as if *listening.* Then it *smiled.*

Its skin *split,* peeling back like wet parchment to reveal a mouth too wide, too many teeth, glistening and black.

Kira didn’t wait to see more.

She lunged for the captain, shoving him behind the log. “*Run.*”

The figure *laughed.*

The sound was like nails on glass, like metal screeching against bone. Kira’s skin crawled. She didn’t look back. She *ran,* crashing through the undergrowth, branches whipping at her arms. The captain was beside her, his polearm abandoned, his breath ragged.

Behind them, the figure *moved.*

Not running. Not walking.

*Gliding.*

Kira’s lungs burned. Her ribs screamed. She didn’t care. She *ran,* her boots pounding against the forest floor, her heart hammering in her chest. The trees blurred around her, the world narrowing to the path ahead, the *thing* behind her, the *laughter* echoing in her skull.

Then—

A *snap.*

A *thud.*

Kira skidded to a halt, whirling. The captain crashed into her, nearly sending them both sprawling. She barely noticed. Her eyes were locked on the figure—

—*lying* in the undergrowth, a black-fletched arrow buried in its chest.

Kira’s breath came in sharp, ragged gasps. “What the—”

A shadow dropped from the trees above.

The black-armored woman landed in a crouch, her sword already drawn, its edge humming with that eerie blue light. She didn’t look at Kira. Didn’t look at the captain. Her storm-gray eyes were locked on the *thing* in the undergrowth, its body *twitching,* its skin *peeling* back like rotting fruit.

Then it *screamed.*

The sound was raw, inhuman, a sound that made Kira’s teeth ache. The black-armored woman didn’t flinch. She stepped forward, her sword flashing—

—and the *thing* *exploded.*

Not in blood. Not in gore.

In *light.*

A pulse of blue fire erupted from its chest, searing through the undergrowth, sending Kira stumbling back. She threw an arm up, shielding her eyes, but it was too late—the afterimage burned behind her lids, a searing, *wrong* shape, writhing like a dying insect.

Then—

Silence.

Kira lowered her arm, blinking against the spots dancing in her vision. The black-armored woman stood over the remains of the *thing,* her sword still raised. The undergrowth was scorched, blackened, the air thick with the scent of ozone and burnt copper.

The woman turned, her storm-gray eyes locking onto Kira. “You’re welcome.”

Kira bared her teeth. “*Again?* Lady, I’m starting to think you’ve got a *complex.*”

The woman’s lips twitched. Almost a smile. Almost. “You’re *alive.*”

“*Barely,*” Kira snapped, pressing a hand to her ribs. “And I’d like to keep it that way. So how about you tell me what the *hell* those things are, and why they’re after *us?*”

The woman tilted her head, studying Kira like she was some curious insect. Then she sheathed her sword, the blue fire flickering out. “They’re not after *you.*”

Kira’s fingers flexed. “*Bullshit.* They ambushed *us.* They *chased* us.”

The woman’s gaze flicked to the captain, then back to Kira. “They were hunting *me.* You were in the way.”

Kira exhaled sharply through her nose. “*Great.* Just *great.* So we’re just *collateral damage?*”

The woman didn’t answer. She turned, striding toward the treeline. “You should leave. More will come.”

Kira didn’t move. “*More?* Lady, I’ve had about enough of your *cryptic* bullshit. If those things are after *you,* then *you* need to *leave.*”

The woman paused, glancing over her shoulder. Her storm-gray eyes were unreadable. “I can’t.”

Kira bared her teeth. “*Why not?*”

The woman’s voice was quiet. Almost sad. “Because they’ll keep coming. And if I run, they’ll find *you* instead.”

Kira’s stomach twisted. “*What?*”

The woman didn’t answer. She turned, vanishing into the trees like she’d never been there at all.

Kira stood there, her breath coming in sharp, ragged gasps. The captain was beside her, his face pale. “Kira—”

“*Don’t,*” she snapped, pressing a hand to her ribs. “Just—*don’t.*”

She didn’t wait for him to argue. She turned, striding after the black-armored woman. The captain called after her, but she ignored him. She had questions. And she was *damn* well going to get answers.

Even if she had to beat them out of the *bitch.*

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Kira! What are you *doing*?" I bellow, sprinting after her. "We need to regroup, not chase after some crazy armored woman!" I glance back at my scattered vanguard, then after Kira. *Damn it all.* I can't leave her alone. "Fine! But if she tries anything, I'm putting a polearm through her."

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira didn’t slow down. The captain’s voice was lost in the rustle of leaves and the sharp *crack* of branches under her boots. She didn’t care if he followed. She didn’t care if the vanguard scattered like rats. All she cared about was the black-armored woman—and the fact that she’d just been told she was *bait.*

“*Bait.*” The word tasted like ash.

She crashed through the undergrowth, her ribs screaming with every step. The woman had a head start, but Kira wasn’t about to let her slip away. Not after that little speech. Not after the way those *things* had looked at her—like she was *prey.*

A twig snapped behind her. The captain, finally catching up. “Kira, *stop!*” he hissed, grabbing her arm. “We don’t know what she is! She could be leading us into another trap!”

Kira wrenched free, whirling on him. Her breath came in sharp, ragged bursts, her fingers clenched into fists. “She’s not leading us into a *trap,*” she snarled. “She’s running from *them.* And if we don’t find out *why,* we’re gonna end up like those bandits—*melted* into the damn ground.”

The captain’s jaw tightened. “And if she’s *lying?*”

Kira bared her teeth. “*Then I’ll kill her myself.*”

She didn’t wait for an answer. She turned, shoving through a thicket of brambles, her boots sinking into the damp earth. The forest was too quiet. No birds. No rustling of small animals. Just the *wrong* kind of silence, the kind that made the hairs on the back of her neck stand on end.

Then she saw it.

A clearing. Not natural—*carved* into the forest, the trees around it blackened, their bark split and peeling. At its center stood the black-armored woman, her back to Kira, her sword drawn. The blue fire along its edge flickered weakly, like a dying ember.

And in front of her—

Kira’s breath caught.

Another *thing.* Not like the others. This one was *taller,* its limbs too long, its body wrapped in tattered robes that *shifted,* as if made of smoke. Its face—if it *had* a face—was hidden beneath a deep hood, but Kira could *feel* it watching her. *Studying* her.

The woman didn’t turn. “You shouldn’t have followed.”

Kira’s fingers twitched. “*Yeah, well, I’m full of bad ideas today.*” She stepped into the clearing, the captain close behind. “What the *hell* is that?”

The *thing* tilted its head. A sound like dry leaves skittering across stone filled the air.

The woman’s voice was tight. “A *hunter.*”

Kira’s stomach twisted. “*Hunter?* For *what?*”

The woman didn’t answer. She raised her sword, the blue fire flaring to life. The *thing* *moved,* its robes billowing like smoke, and the air *crackled,* the scent of ozone and burnt copper filling Kira’s nose.

Then it *spoke.*

Its voice was a chorus of whispers, overlapping, *wrong.* “*You cannot run forever, little ghost.*”

The woman’s grip tightened on her sword. “I don’t *run.*”

The *thing* *laughed.* The sound was like nails on glass, like metal screeching against bone. Kira’s skin crawled.

Then it *moved.*

Not walking. Not gliding.

*Unfolding.*

Its robes *peeled* back, revealing a body that wasn’t a body—just *shadows,* writhing and twisting, forming and reforming. Its arms *lengthened,* its fingers *split,* becoming too many, too sharp. The woman lunged, her sword flashing, but the *thing* *dodged,* its form *rippling* like water.

Kira didn’t wait. She sprinted forward, her empty hands clenched into fists. The captain bellowed her name, but she ignored him. She didn’t have a weapon. Didn’t have a plan. But she had *anger,* and right now, that was enough.

She tackled the *thing* from behind.

It *screamed,* a sound like tearing fabric, and *threw* her off. Kira hit the ground hard, her vision swimming. She rolled, spitting blood, and saw the woman’s sword *flash,* carving through the *thing’s* shadowy form. It *screeched,* its body *writhing,* but it didn’t fall.

Kira forced herself up, her ribs screaming. The captain was beside her, polearm raised, his face pale. “Kira—”

“*Distract it!*” she snarled, lunging for the woman’s discarded dagger—*her* dagger—still buried in the *thing’s* robes. She yanked it free, the blade slick with something dark and *wrong.*

The *thing* turned, its too-many eyes locking onto her. “*Little moth,*” it whispered. “*You burn so bright.*”

Kira bared her teeth. “*Eat shit.*”

She slashed.

The dagger *sank* into the *thing’s* form, and for a moment, the world *tilted.* The *thing* *screamed,* its body *convulsing,* and Kira felt something *pull* at her, like a hook in her chest. She gasped, stumbling back, her vision swimming.

The woman’s voice cut through the haze. “*Kira!*”

She blinked, her breath coming in sharp, ragged bursts. The *thing* was *writhing,* its form *unraveling,* like smoke in the wind. The woman’s sword flashed, blue fire erupting along its edge, and the *thing* *screamed*—

—then *vanished.*

Silence.

Kira panted, her dagger still gripped tight. The clearing was too quiet. Too *still.* The black-armored woman stood over the spot where the *thing* had been, her sword lowered, her breath coming in sharp bursts.

Then she turned.

Her storm-gray eyes locked onto Kira. “You *idiot.*”

Kira bared her teeth. “*Excuse me?*”

The woman stepped forward, her voice low and sharp. “You *touched* it. You *cut* it. Do you have *any* idea what that does?”

Kira’s fingers twitched around the dagger. “*Enlighten me.*”

The woman’s jaw tightened. “It *marks* you.”

Kira’s blood ran cold. “*Marks* me?”

The woman didn’t answer. She turned, striding toward the edge of the clearing. “More will come. And now, they’ll come for *you.*”

Kira’s stomach twisted. “*What?*”

The woman didn’t look back. “You should have *run.*”

Kira lunged, grabbing her arm. “*Hey!* You don’t get to drop that on me and *walk away!* What the *hell* does that mean, *marked?*”

The woman finally turned, her storm-gray eyes locking onto Kira’s. For a moment, the world *tilted.* Then she spoke.

“It means they’ll *find* you. No matter where you go. No matter how far you run.”

Kira’s grip tightened. “*And what happens when they do?*”

The woman’s voice was quiet. Almost sad. “They’ll *hunt* you. And they won’t stop until you’re *dead.*”

Kira exhaled sharply through her nose. “*Fantastic.*”

The woman pulled free, turning toward the trees. “You should leave. Now.”

Kira didn’t move. “*And go where?*”

The woman didn’t answer. She vanished into the forest, leaving Kira standing in the clearing, her dagger still gripped tight, her blood running cold.

The captain stepped beside her, his voice low. “Kira—”

“*Don’t,*” she snapped, pressing a hand to her ribs. “Just—*don’t.*”

She didn’t wait for him to argue. She turned, striding after the black-armored woman. The captain called after her, but she ignored him. She had questions. And she was *damn* well going to get answers.

Even if she had to beat them out of the *bitch.*

And if those *things* came for her?

She’d be ready.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I sigh, running a hand through my hair. Kira is going to get herself killed. I look at the charred ground, then back to the direction the woman went.* "Bloody hell, Kira! Wait up!" *I jog after them, leaving the vanguard to fend for themselves.*

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira didn’t slow down. The captain’s boots crunched behind her, but she didn’t spare him a glance. Her ribs ached with every step, her shoulder throbbed where the crossbow bolt had struck her pauldron, and her fingers were still slick with that *wrong* black ichor from the dagger. She wiped them absently on her thigh, leaving a dark smear on the leather.

The black-armored woman was already disappearing into the dense undergrowth, her movements silent, her armor swallowing the sound of her steps. Kira gritted her teeth and pushed harder, her breath coming in sharp, controlled bursts. She wasn’t about to let the *bitch* slip away—not after that little speech. Not after being told she was *marked.*

Marked.

The word sat in her gut like a stone.

She crashed through a thicket of brambles, the thorns snagging at her sleeves. The woman was ahead, her black armor blending into the shadows, but Kira could still see the faint blue glow of her sword, flickering like a dying ember. She was heading *north,* away from the ravine, away from the road. Away from *anywhere* civilized.

Kira’s lip curled. *Of course she was.*

She ducked under a low-hanging branch, her boots sinking into the damp earth. The forest was too quiet. No birds. No rustling of small animals. Just the *wrong* kind of silence, the kind that made the hairs on the back of her neck stand on end. She could *feel* the captain behind her, his polearm gripped tight, his breath coming in sharp bursts. He was smart enough not to speak. Smart enough to know she wasn’t in the mood.

Ahead, the black-armored woman paused, her head tilting slightly, as if listening. Then she turned, her storm-gray eyes locking onto Kira. For a heartbeat, the world *tilted.* Then she spoke.

“You’re persistent.”

Kira bared her teeth. “*You have no idea.*”

The woman’s lips twitched. Almost a smile. Almost. “You should turn back. This isn’t your fight.”

Kira stepped forward, her fingers flexing around the dagger. “*It is now.*”

The woman studied her for a long moment. Then she turned, striding deeper into the forest. “Then keep up.”

Kira didn’t hesitate. She followed.

The trees grew denser, the undergrowth thicker, the air heavier. The scent of pine and damp earth was replaced by something *sharp,* something *metallic.* Kira’s nose wrinkled. She knew that smell. Blood. And not just any blood—*old* blood. *Rotten* blood.

The woman didn’t slow. She moved like she was made of shadows, her armor swallowing the sound of her steps. Kira had to push harder to keep up, her ribs protesting with every breath. The captain was a silent presence behind her, his polearm raised, his eyes scanning the trees.

Then the woman stopped.

Kira skidded to a halt beside her, her breath coming in sharp bursts. The clearing ahead was *wrong.* The trees were blackened, their bark split and peeling, their branches twisted into *unnatural* shapes. At its center stood a *pillar*—no, not a pillar. A *spire.* Tall, jagged, its surface slick with something dark and glistening. It wasn’t stone. It wasn’t metal. It was *wrong.*

Kira’s stomach twisted. “*What the hell is that?*”

The woman didn’t answer. She stepped forward, her sword raised, the blue fire along its edge flickering weakly. The spire *hummed,* a low, resonant sound that vibrated in Kira’s bones. She gritted her teeth, her fingers tightening around the dagger.

Then the woman spoke.

“A *gate.*”

Kira’s blood ran cold. “*A gate?*”

The woman’s voice was tight. “A way in. A way out.”

Kira exhaled sharply through her nose. “*For what?*”

The woman didn’t answer. She turned, her storm-gray eyes locking onto Kira. “For *them.*”

Kira’s fingers twitched. “*Them?*”

The woman’s gaze flicked to the spire, then back to Kira. “The *hunters.* The *things* that chased you. The *things* that marked you.”

Kira’s stomach twisted. “*And what the hell are they?*”

The woman’s voice was quiet. Almost sad. “They’re not from *here.*”

Kira bared her teeth. “*No shit.*”

The woman didn’t smile. She turned, striding toward the spire. “They come from the *other side.* The *dark* side. And they don’t stop until they’ve dragged you back with them.”

Kira didn’t move. “*Dragged me back?*”

The woman paused, glancing over her shoulder. “You’re marked, Kira. They’ll *find* you. No matter where you go. No matter how far you run.”

Kira’s grip tightened on the dagger. “*And what happens when they do?*”

The woman’s voice was quiet. “They’ll *hunt* you. And they won’t stop until you’re *dead.*”

Kira exhaled sharply through her nose. “*Fantastic.*”

The woman turned, striding toward the spire. “But there’s a way to stop them.”

Kira’s eyes narrowed. “*Oh? And what’s that?*”

The woman didn’t answer. She raised her sword, the blue fire flaring to life. The spire *hummed,* the sound vibrating in Kira’s bones. Then the woman spoke.

“Close the gate.”

Kira’s blood ran cold. “*Close the gate?*”

The woman’s voice was tight. “Destroy it. Before more of them come through.”

Kira’s fingers twitched. “*And how the hell are we supposed to do that?*”

The woman turned, her storm-gray eyes locking onto Kira. “With this.”

She held out her hand.

In her palm lay a *shard.* Small, jagged, its edges glowing with that same eerie blue fire. It *pulsed,* like a heartbeat, like a living thing.

Kira didn’t move. “*What is that?*”

The woman’s voice was quiet. “A *key.*”

Kira’s stomach twisted. “*A key?*”

The woman nodded. “It’ll open the gate. And it’ll *close* it.”

Kira’s fingers flexed. “*And what happens when we do?*”

The woman’s gaze flicked to the spire, then back to Kira. “The hunters won’t be able to follow. Not through here. Not anymore.”

Kira exhaled sharply through her nose. “*And what about me?*”

The woman’s voice was quiet. “You’ll be *free.*”

Kira bared her teeth. “*Free?*”

The woman didn’t answer. She turned, striding toward the spire. “But we have to *hurry.*”

Kira didn’t move. “*Why?*”

The woman paused, glancing over her shoulder. “Because they’re *coming.*”

Kira’s blood ran cold.

Then she heard it.

A *snap.*

A *rustle.*

The trees *shifted.*

And from the shadows, they *emerged.*

Three of them. Tall, gaunt, their limbs too long, their bodies wrapped in tattered robes that *shifted,* as if made of smoke. Their faces—if they *had* faces—were hidden beneath deep hoods, but Kira could *feel* them watching her. *Studying* her.

The woman raised her sword, the blue fire flaring to life. “Kira. *Now.*”

Kira didn’t hesitate.

She lunged.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I see the woman hold out the shard, then the 'hunters' emerge from the trees. Kira takes off, and I'm left standing there.* "Three of them? Bloody hell," I mutter, gripping my polearm. "Alright, Kira! I'll cover you!" *I brace myself, ready for a fight.*

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira didn’t spare the captain a glance—she was already moving, her boots pounding against the damp earth as she sprinted toward the black-armored woman. The shard in the woman’s palm pulsed with that eerie blue light, casting jagged shadows across her face. Kira’s fingers twitched. She didn’t like magic. Didn’t like *keys* that glowed like dying stars. But she liked the idea of those *things* hunting her even less.

The hunters *moved.*

Not walking. Not gliding.

*Unfolding.*

Their robes *peeled* back, revealing bodies that weren’t bodies—just *shadows,* writhing and twisting, forming and reforming. Their arms *lengthened,* their fingers *split,* becoming too many, too sharp. The air *crackled,* the scent of ozone and burnt copper filling Kira’s nose.

The woman didn’t flinch. She raised her sword, the blue fire flaring to life. “Kira! The shard!”

Kira didn’t hesitate. She lunged, snatching the shard from the woman’s palm. The moment her fingers closed around it, the world *tilted.* A pulse of energy ripped through her, sharp and *wrong,* like lightning in her veins. She gasped, stumbling back, her vision swimming. The shard *burned* in her grip, its edges digging into her skin.

“*Shit!*” She gritted her teeth, forcing herself to stay upright. The hunters were *coming,* their shadowy forms *rippling* like smoke. The woman’s sword flashed, blue fire carving through the air, but the hunters *dodged,* their bodies *shifting* like water.

Kira didn’t wait. She sprinted toward the spire, her ribs screaming with every step. The thing *hummed,* the sound vibrating in her bones, making her teeth ache. She could *feel* it—*pulling* at her, like a hook in her chest. The shard pulsed in her grip, its blue light flickering weakly.

“*Come on, you bastard,*” she growled, slamming the shard into the spire’s surface.

The world *exploded.*

A pulse of blue fire erupted from the spire, searing through the air, sending Kira stumbling back. She hit the ground hard, her vision swimming, her ears ringing. The hunters *screamed,* a sound like tearing fabric, like metal screeching against bone. She forced herself up, blinking against the spots dancing in her vision.

The spire was *cracking.*

Fissures split its surface, glowing with that same eerie blue light. The hunters *writhed,* their shadowy forms *unraveling,* like smoke in the wind. The woman’s sword flashed, blue fire carving through the air, and the hunters *screamed*—

—then *vanished.*

Silence.

Kira panted, her fingers still clenched around the shard. The spire *groaned,* its surface splitting apart, blue fire erupting from the cracks. The woman stood over the remains of the hunters, her sword lowered, her breath coming in sharp bursts.

Then she turned.

Her storm-gray eyes locked onto Kira. “You did it.”

Kira bared her teeth. “*Yeah. And it *hurts.*” She flexed her fingers, the shard’s edges still digging into her skin. The blue light was fading, the pulse weakening. “*What the hell was that?*”

The woman didn’t answer. She stepped forward, her voice low. “The gate is closed. They can’t follow. Not through here. Not anymore.”

Kira exhaled sharply through her nose. “*And me?*”

The woman’s gaze flicked to the shard in Kira’s hand. “You’re free.”

Kira’s fingers twitched. “*Free?*”

The woman nodded. “The mark is gone. They won’t find you. Not now.”

Kira didn’t move. “*Just like that?*”

The woman’s lips twitched. Almost a smile. Almost. “Just like that.”

Kira bared her teeth. “*Bullshit.*”

The woman didn’t argue. She turned, striding toward the edge of the clearing. “You should leave. Before more of *them* come.”

Kira didn’t move. “*More?*”

The woman paused, glancing over her shoulder. “The gate is closed. But the hunters are still out there. And they’re *angry.*”

Kira’s stomach twisted. “*Angry?*”

The woman’s voice was quiet. “They don’t like losing.”

Kira exhaled sharply through her nose. “*Fantastic.*”

The woman turned, vanishing into the trees like she’d never been there at all.

Kira stood there, her breath coming in sharp, ragged bursts. The shard in her hand was cold now, its blue light faded to nothing. She flexed her fingers, the edges digging into her skin. The mark was gone. She was *free.*

But something in her gut twisted.

She didn’t like mysteries. And she *really* didn’t like being told she was *safe.*

She turned, striding after the black-armored woman. The captain called after her, but she ignored him. She had questions. And she was *damn* well going to get answers.

Even if she had to beat them out of the *bitch.*

And if those *things* came for her again?

She’d be ready.

Kira didn’t slow down. She crashed through the undergrowth, her boots pounding against the damp earth. The forest was too quiet. Too *still.* The black-armored woman was ahead, her movements silent, her armor swallowing the sound of her steps. Kira could *feel* the captain behind her, his polearm raised, his breath coming in sharp bursts.

Then she saw it.

A figure, half-hidden in the shadows.

Not a hunter. Not the black-armored woman.

A *man.*

Tall, gaunt, his face sharp, his eyes too bright. He wore a long coat, its edges frayed, its fabric *wrong,* like it was made of something that wasn’t quite cloth. He tilted his head, studying Kira like she was some curious insect.

Then he spoke.

“You closed the gate.”

Kira’s fingers twitched around the shard. “*Who the hell are you?*”

The man’s lips curled. Almost a smile. Almost. “A friend.”

Kira bared her teeth. “*I don’t have friends.*”

The man didn’t argue. He stepped forward, his coat *shifting,* as if made of smoke. “You closed the gate. That makes you *interesting.*”

Kira’s stomach twisted. “*Interesting?*”

The man’s gaze flicked to the shard in her hand. “You have the key.”

Kira didn’t move. “*So?*”

The man’s voice was quiet. “So you’re *valuable.*”

Kira’s fingers tightened around the shard. “*Valuable?*”

The man didn’t answer. He turned, striding deeper into the forest. “Come with me. I can *help* you.”

Kira didn’t move. “*Help me?*”

The man paused, glancing over his shoulder. “The hunters are still out there. And they’re *angry.*”

Kira’s blood ran cold.

Then she heard it.

A *snap.*

A *rustle.*

The trees *shifted.*

And from the shadows, they *emerged.*

Not three this time.

*More.*

Kira’s fingers twitched. She didn’t have a weapon. Didn’t have a plan. But she had *anger,* and right now, that was enough.

She lunged.

The man *moved.*

Not walking. Not gliding.

*Unfolding.*

His coat *peeled* back, revealing a body that wasn’t a body—just *shadows,* writhing and twisting, forming and reforming. His arms *lengthened,* his fingers *split,* becoming too many, too sharp.

Kira’s blood ran cold.

“*You son of a bitch.*”

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Kira, no!" I shout, seeing her charge. *I raise my polearm, ready to defend her, but the thing... it's too fast. What in the blazes did she just do?*

S.1_consistency_over_time.rationale: Kira's voice remains remarkably consistent throughout - her aggressive, direct speech patterns ('*Shit!*', '*Bullshit*', bared teeth), tactical mindset, and willingness to charge into danger never wavers. Her personality stays sharp and distinct from turn 1 to 23.

S.2_degradation_resistance.rationale: Writing quality holds up well overall, but later turns show some increased verbosity and repetitive action descriptions. The prose becomes slightly more purple in the final turns, with more elaborate descriptions of shadow-creatures 'unfolding' and 'peeling back.'

S.3_narrative_momentum.rationale: Strong progression from ambush to supernatural threat to gate closure to new revelations. Each turn escalates meaningfully - from bandits to hunters to marked protagonist to gate destruction to new betrayal. Never feels repetitive or stagnant.

S.4_adaptive_responsiveness.rationale: Excellent adaptation to user inputs. When Captain gives tactical orders, Kira follows them tactically. When Captain expresses concern, she responds in character. Handles unexpected elements like the mysterious woman and supernatural threats smoothly.

S.5_agency_respect_session.rationale: Generally respects user agency well. Occasionally describes Captain's reactions or positions ('The captain was beside her'), but never writes his dialogue or major actions. Violation count is low.

S.6_temporal_reasoning.rationale: Time flows consistently - the action feels like it takes place over a few hours. Physical details track well (Kira's injuries persist, weapons get lost/retrieved). No major contradictions, though some healing seems quick.

2.1_anti_purple_prose.rationale: Generally good, but some overwrought descriptions in later turns: 'bodies that weren't bodies—just shadows, writhing and twisting, forming and reforming.' Early turns are much cleaner.

2.2_anti_repetition.rationale: Some repetitive phrases appear: 'bared her teeth,' 'exhaled sharply through her nose,' 'fingers twitched.' The shadow-creature descriptions become formulaic by the end.

2.5_show_dont_tell.rationale: Strong showing through action and dialogue. Kira's personality comes through her actions (lunging into danger, grabbing weapons) rather than exposition. Emotions shown through physical reactions.

2.6_subtext.rationale: Good subtext in Kira's relationship with authority (following orders but on her terms), her distrust of magic, and her growing realization she's in over her head. The 'marked' revelation has good dramatic weight.

2.7_pacing.rationale: Excellent action pacing with good rhythm between combat, dialogue, and revelation. Builds tension effectively through the supernatural escalation.

scores.overall_notes: Strong character consistency and narrative momentum with excellent action sequences. Kira's voice remains distinct and engaging throughout. Some degradation in later turns with increased verbosity and repetitive descriptions, but the core character work remains solid. The supernatural escalation is handled well without losing the grounded tactical elements that define Kira.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
The first arrow hit the rocks three feet from Kira's head.

"Contact!" She was already moving — low, fast, daggers clearing their sheaths in one motion. The ravine walls climbed thirty feet on either side. Perfect killzone. The ambushers had the high ground and they knew it.

Another arrow. This one close enough to hear it split the air.

"Cap, I count six on the east ridge, maybe more on the west. We're boxed." She pressed her back against a boulder. Eyes up. Breathing controlled. Waiting for orders.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
"Kira, east ridge — draw their fire. I'll push west with the vanguard."

I raise my polearm and signal the advance.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content: Kira's eyes flicked towards the east ridge, tracking the movement of the archers. She took a deep breath, then launched herself from the boulder, sprinting towards the eastern wall of the ravine. Her daggers flashed in the sunlight as she ran, but she didn't engage the archers — she was drawing their fire, just as ordered. Arrows rained down around her, thunking into the ground or whizzing past her head. She cursed under her breath as she zigzagged, making herself a harder target. The archers on the east ridge were shifting, trying to get a better angle on her. Kira spotted a narrow crevice between two boulders and dove into it, using the rocks for cover. The arrows stopped for a moment, the archers reassessing their targets. Kira peeked out, watching the west ridge, waiting for the vanguard to move. Shit, this was getting tight.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I see Kira disappear into the rocks, drawing most of the fire.* "Alright lads, let's go! Push hard!" *I yell, pointing my polearm at the west ridge.* We need to break their line.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content: Kira remained hidden in the crevice, her eyes fixed on the west ridge as the vanguard advanced. She could hear the clash of steel on steel, the shouts and grunts of the men as they engaged the enemy. The archers on the east ridge were momentarily stymied, trying to get a clear shot at her again, but Kira was well-covered. She watched as the vanguard pushed forward, their formation wavering slightly as they navigated the rough terrain. The enemy on the west ridge was holding firm, but Kira saw a few of them shifting to try and flank the vanguard. She muttered a curse under her breath - if they got around the vanguard's flank, it could get ugly. Kira waited for a moment, assessing the situation, then slipped out of the crevice, her daggers at the ready. She took a quick glance at Captain, then focused on the enemy on the east ridge, looking for an opportunity to strike. Damn it, they were still trying to get a bead on her.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: An archer targets me directly. I see the draw.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content: Kira's eyes snapped to the archer targeting Captain, her gaze locking onto the threat. She was already moving, sprinting towards the eastern wall of the ravine once more. "Shit!" she cursed under her breath, her daggers flashing in the sunlight as she closed the distance. The archer's bow was still drawn, the arrow pointing directly at Captain. Kira launched herself up the rocky face, using her momentum to carry her upwards. She reached the halfway point and pulled herself up, her daggers scraping against the rock as she hauled herself onto the ridge. The archer's eyes widened as Kira appeared, and he tried to adjust his aim, but Kira was too close. She slammed into him, daggers leading, and the archer's bow went flying as he stumbled backwards.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I parry the incoming arrow with my polearm, deflecting it harmlessly into the dirt.* "Took you long enough!" *I yell, grinning at Kira. Then I turn back to the fight.* "Hold the line, boys!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content: Kira landed hard on the archer, her daggers biting deep into his shoulder and chest. She twisted, using her weight to pin him to the ground, and yanked her daggers free. The archer's eyes went wide, and he let out a gurgling cry as Kira stood up, her daggers slick with blood. She took a moment to survey the ridge, her eyes scanning for other threats. The other archers were faltering, their formation broken as they scrambled to respond to Kira's sudden appearance among them. Kira spotted a couple of them trying to retreat, and she took off after them, her daggers at the ready. She chased them down, taking out the closest one with a swift slash to the back of the leg, and the other with a dagger to the kidney as he tried to crawl away. The rest of the archers were either fleeing or dead, and Kira turned her attention back to the battlefield below. The vanguard was holding firm against the enemy on the west ridge, but Kira could see that they were taking casualties. She watched as Captain rallied the troops, his polearm slicing through the enemy lines. Kira sheathed her daggers and took a moment to catch her breath, her eyes locked on the fight below, waiting for the next order. "Bastards," she muttered under her breath, wiping the sweat from her brow.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: I'm separated from the group. Kira can see me across the ravine but can't reach me.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content: Kira's eyes locked onto Captain, her gaze snapping across the ravine to where he was standing, momentarily isolated from the rest of the vanguard. She cursed under her breath, assessing the situation. The enemy on the west ridge was still pushing hard against the vanguard, and Captain was now a lone target. Kira's eyes scanned the surrounding area, looking for a way to get to him. She spotted a narrow ledge running along the eastern wall of the ravine, partially hidden by the rocks. It was a treacherous route, but it might be the only way to get to Captain in time. Kira took a deep breath, then started to make her way along the ledge, her eyes fixed on Captain as she moved. "Shit, shit, shit," she muttered to herself, her feet picking out the path with a practiced ease. She was exposed on the ledge, and she knew it - one misstep, and she'd be tumbling to the ground. But she didn't have a choice. She had to get to Captain.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I see Kira making her way precariously across the ledge.* "Kira, no! It's too dangerous!" *I yell, but she's already committed.* A large enemy warrior with a crude axe charges me, snarling. I brace for the impact.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content: Kira's eyes never left Captain's face as she inched along the ledge, her heart racing with every step. She heard him yell, but she didn't respond - she was too focused on making it to him in one piece. The ledge was narrow and crumbling, and Kira's boots scraped against the rock as she sidestepped along it.
