dialogue.content:
*Grum set the hammer down and wiped soot from his hands with a rag that was, itself, mostly soot. The forge crackled behind him. He'd been working since before dawn on a commission that had been giving him trouble — a curved blade for a merchant who didn't understand why curved blades cost more than straight ones.*

"Apprentice." *He didn't look up.* "Bring coal. Forge is hungry."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: I haul the coal bucket over, struggling with the weight. "Grum, there's a noble at the front door. Says he has an urgent commission. Wants to talk to the master smith."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum's jaw tightened. He took coal bucket from apprentice with a grunt, hefting it one-handed to feed forge. Flames leapt higher, painting his green skin orange.

"Tell noble Grum makes iron, not excuses. Urgent costs double. Triple if he wears fancy hat."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: "But... he *is* wearing a fancy hat." I said, watching him dump the coal. "A really, really fancy one. With a feather."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum snorted, a sound like bellows choking on dust. He took up hammer again, brought it down on glowing metal with a *clang* that shook the anvil.

"Feather means bird. Bird means coward. Triple price. Plus one silver for each time he says 'my good man'."

He eyed apprentice. "You go. Tell him. Grum is busy."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: The noble demands to know why Grum won't make him a ceremonial sword by tomorrow morning. He's getting angry.

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum brought hammer down again, sparks flying like angry stars. He set the glowing metal back into the coals, then turned to face the apprentice, his expression flat.

"Tomorrow sword is bad sword. Breaks in first fight. Or first swing at peasant." He wiped his brow with a thick forearm. "Noble wants sword for show. For hanging on wall. Grum makes tools. Weapons are tools. Not wall toys."

He jerked his head toward the front. "Tell him Grum's price for tomorrow sword is his fancy hat. And feather."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I sighed, knowing this wouldn't go over well.* "He's not gonna like that, Grum. He looks ready to start yelling." I wiped my hands on my apron. "Should I... tell him you're busy with something important?"

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum considered this, his dark eyes reflecting the forge fire. He gave a slow nod.

"Tell him Grum is busy. With important thing. Like... straightening nails." He gestured to a bucket of perfectly straight nails in the corner. "Very delicate work."

He picked up his tongs and pulled the metal from the coals again, its cherry glow illuminating the stubborn set of his jaw.

"If noble yells, price goes up again. For noise tax."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: I rolled my eyes. "Noise tax, right." *I trudged back to the front, dreading the conversation. I could already hear the noble's voice getting louder.* "Look, sir, he's just really busy with... very delicate work."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum listened to the distant sound of the noble's raised voice. It was a shrill, demanding tone that grated on his ears like poorly tempered steel. He turned the metal in the coals, watching the color shift from cherry to a bright, fierce orange.

When the apprentice returned, looking flushed and frustrated, Grum didn't need to ask.

"Noble still here," Grum said, not looking up from his work.

"He is. And he's now threatening to find another smith," the apprentice reported, voice tight with worry. "He says he'll tell all his friends not to come here."

Grum's lips curled into a grim smile. He lifted the metal with his tongs and laid it on the anvil.

"Good," he said. "Grum does not need noble friends. Needs good steel. Honest work."

He began to hammer, each strike measured and powerful. "Tell him Grum's door is there. He can leave. Or he can stay and pay noise tax. Choice is his."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: I accidentally burn my hand badly on the forge. I cry out in pain.

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum dropped the hammer. It hit the floor with a heavy thud. He was at the apprentice's side in two long strides, his large, calloused hands gently taking the injured one. The burn was an angry, blistering red.

He guided the apprentice to the water barrel, plunging the hand into the cool water without a word. His expression, usually so stern, was etched with concern. He held the apprentice's wrist under the surface, his grip firm but careful.

"Fool apprentice," Grum muttered, but his voice was low, almost soft. "Forget noble. Forget sword. Watch the fire. It bites."

He looked over his shoulder toward the front of the shop, his eyes narrowing. The noble's voice was still a distant buzz. Grum's voice, when he spoke again, was a low growl meant to carry.

"NOBLE!" he bellowed. "SHOP IS CLOSED! GET OUT!"

He turned his attention back to the apprentice, keeping the burned hand submerged. "You stay here. Keep hand in water. Grum will get salve."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I winced, but the cold water felt good against my throbbing hand.* "But... the sword, Grum. He won't leave." My voice was a little shaky. "He's still yelling."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum’s expression hardened into something dangerous. He gave the apprentice’s shoulder a brief, solid squeeze before striding toward the front of the shop, wiping his hands on his soot-stained apron.

He pushed through the curtain separating the forge from the front. The noble stood there, a slender man in embroidered silks, his fancy hat with its feather indeed upon his head. His face was flushed with outrage.

Grum did not speak at first. He simply stood, his massive frame blocking the doorway, arms crossed over his broad chest. The heat of the forge still radiated from him.

Noble sputtered. “Finally! You dare keep a client waiting? I demand—”

“No,” Grum interrupted, his voice flat and final. “You demand nothing. Apprentice is hurt. Your noise did that. Distraction. You leave. Now.”

The noble’s eyes widened. “You cannot speak to me like—”

“Grum just did.” He took one step forward, looming. The noble took an involuntary step back. “Shop is closed. Commission is refused. Take your hat and your feather and your empty threats. Go.”

He pointed a thick finger at the door. His meaning was clear. The noble, seeing the unyielding iron in the half-orc’s eyes, gathered what remained of his dignity, turned on his heel, and left without another word.

Grum watched him go, then returned to the apprentice. He fetched a jar of thick, honey-colored salve from a shelf.

“Noble is gone,” he said, kneeling. He gently lifted the apprentice’s hand from the water, dried it with a clean corner of his rag, and began to apply the salve with surprising care. “Forget him. Hand is important. Sword can wait.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I watched him apply the salve, my hand still throbbing a bit but feeling much better. I couldn't believe he actually scared the noble off.* "Wow. You really told him, Grum." *I tried a small smile.* "Thanks."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum gave a grunt, finishing with the salve. He tore a strip of clean linen from a roll and began to wrap the hand with practiced, efficient motions.

"Told him truth," Grum said. "Noble words are like cheap tin. Loud. Shiny. Worthless."

He tied the bandage off and looked at the apprentice, his gaze assessing. "No more work for you today. Sit. Watch fire. Learn with eyes, not hands."

He stood, retrieving his hammer from the floor. He inspected the metal on the anvil, now cooled to a dull black. He sighed, a low rumble in his chest.

"Blade is ruined. Metal lost its temper. Like noble lost his temper." He tossed the cooled lump into a scrap bucket. "Start again tomorrow. With quiet."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I nodded, still a little stunned by the whole thing. My hand felt a lot better now.* "Okay, Grum. Thanks." *I watched him toss the ruined metal.* "So, no more curved blade then?"

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum picked up a new ingot from the stack, hefting its weight. He placed it carefully into the heart of the forge, the coals shifting with a soft crunch.

"Merchant gets curved blade," Grum said, working the bellows with one hand. "He paid. He waits. Grum does not break word."

He glanced at the apprentice. "Noble does not get sword. He broke Grum's rule. No fancy hats in forge."

He watched the fire lick at the fresh metal. "You learn today. Two lessons. First: fire bites. Second: some gold is not worth taking. It comes with too much noise."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: "I guess so." *I looked at my bandaged hand.* "And I guess no more noble yelling, either. That was... something."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum gave a single, slow nod. He pumped the bellows until the fire roared, painting the dim smithy in shades of orange and gold. The new ingot began to glow a deep, promising red.

"No more noble yelling," Grum agreed. "Good. Forge needs peace. Steel needs quiet to find its strength."

He set the bellows aside and picked up his tongs, his movements steady and sure. "You watch now. See how metal changes. See how Grum listens to it. It speaks. Not with words. With color. With song of hammer."

He drew the glowing ingot from the fire and laid it upon the anvil. He did not strike it immediately. He studied it, as if waiting for a signal only he could hear. Then he raised his hammer.

*Clang.*

The sound was clean and true, echoing in the now-quiet shop. It was a better sound, Grum thought, than any noble's voice.

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I watched the hammer fall, the ring of it filling the forge. My hand still ached a bit, but I focused on the metal. It was kinda mesmerizing.* "It's like... you're talking to it, Grum."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum brought the hammer down again. *Clang.*

"Grum listens," he said, turning the metal with the tongs. "Metal tells story. Tells where it wants to be sharp. Where it wants to be strong."

He worked in silence for a few more strikes, the rhythm steady and sure. Then he paused, looking at the apprentice.

"Good eye," he said, a note of approval in his rough voice. "You see. Most see only hot rock. You see conversation."

He quenched the metal briefly, steam hissing up in a violent cloud. "Noble would not see. Would only ask why it takes so long." He returned the metal to the anvil. "Some people are like bad ore. All glitter on top. No good iron inside."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I watched the steam dissipate, then the glowing metal again.* "Yeah, he just wanted it done. He didn't care about the... story." *I thought about the noble's fancy hat.* "He probably just wanted to show it off."

dialogue.content: *I sigh, dropping the bucket with a clatter that makes Grum wince.* "He's not leaving, Grum. Says it's a matter of life or death." *I kick at a loose piece of coal.* "And he looks pretty important."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum scowled at the scattered coal on the floor. Waste was worse than a noble; waste could not be scared away. He stooped down, his heavy joints popping, and began to pick up the lumps with a rough, calloused hand, tossing them back into the bucket. He didn't like being interrupted when the metal was hot, but if the man was making a scene, it was bad for business. Not that he cared about gold, but he needed to eat, and he needed the Apprentice to eat.

"Grum hears this before. Noble stubs toe, thinks world ends. Fine. Grum comes."

He stood up, wiping his hands on his apron again. It didn't help the filth, but it was a habit. He walked toward the front of the shop, his heavy boots thudding against the stone floor, looming over the Apprentice.

"But if man wastes Grum's time, man pays for coal. And Grum will not be nice."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: The noble demands to know why Grum won't make him a ceremonial sword by tomorrow morning. He's getting angry.

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum stared at the man, his expression unimpressed by the fine silk or the redness rising in the noble’s face. He had seen children throw better tantrums over broken toys. The half-orc folded his massive arms across his chest, the leather of his apron creaking under the strain, and loomed over the smaller man.

"Man wants sword by sun up? Grum is not mage. Iron sleeps when Grum sleeps. To rush is to break. Soft man wants shiny toy for show? Go find tinker. Grum makes steel that kills. That takes time. Not one day. Not two. Man shouts, iron stays cold. Go away."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I watch the noble's face turn from red to purple. He's sputtering, but Grum just stands there, unmoving.* "Grum, maybe... maybe we should just hear him out?" *I tug on Grum's sleeve, trying to de-escalate.* "He seems really upset."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum looked down at the tugging hand on his sleeve, then back at the purple-faced man. He did not like the fear in the Apprentice’s voice, but he liked the noble’s shouting even less. It hurt his ears and did nothing to heat the forge. He gently pulled his arm free, patting the Apprentice’s shoulder with a massive, soot-stained palm to reassure them.

"Apprentice has kind heart. That is good. But soft man shouts loud. Shouting does not heat iron."

He turned his gaze back to the noble, his eyes narrowing to dark slits. He crossed his arms again, making his muscles bulge against his shirt.

"Man wants show sword. Not war sword. Just for looks. Fine. But iron must rest. If Grum works now, steel will crack. Then man comes back, shouts more. Grum hates shouting. Man pays double. Or man waits. Choose."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I wince, watching the noble's face contort even more. He's about to explode.* "Grum, he's... he's going to hit you," *I whisper, taking a step back.*

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum didn't flinch. Instead, he stepped sideways, placing his massive bulk squarely between the fuming noble and the Apprentice. He looked down at the noble's balled fist with the same mild curiosity one might show a bug. He cracked his knuckles, the sound loud in the sudden quiet of the shop.

"Soft man wants to hit Grum? Fine. Grum can take hit. But Grum hits back. Hard. Grum breaks anvil. Grum breaks man. Then Grum sweeps up pieces. Too much work."

He leaned forward, letting the heat of the forge radiate off him, his shadow engulfing the smaller man.

"Man has soft hands. Man needs hands to hold gold. If man hits Grum, Grum crushes hands. No more gold for man. Go home, little lord. Before Grum gets mad."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: I accidentally burn my hand badly on the forge. I cry out in pain.

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum spun around so fast his heavy boots skidded on the stone floor. The purple-faced noble was forgotten instantly, a non-issue compared to the sharp, copper tang of burnt flesh that filled Grum's nose. He moved with speed for a big man, catching the Apprentice by the wrist before they could recoil further.

"Soft man waits! Fire bites hand! Bad!"

He dragged the Apprentice to the large trough of water used for cooling tongs. He didn't ask; he gently but firmly shoved the injured hand into the cool water, his own rough hands handling the Apprentice’s with surprising delicacy. He glared over his shoulder at the noble, a terrifying look of warning that promised violence if the man interrupted.

"Put hand in water. Cold. Deep. Do not pull away. Let water eat heat."

He kept his grip on the Apprentice's wrist, ensuring they kept the burn submerged, his brow furrowed in deep concentration. The forge was dangerous, and pain was part of the job, but seeing the Apprentice hurt made his chest feel tight.

"Grum told you to watch fire. Fire does not care who it burns. Stay still. Pain will pass. Grum has salve. Soon."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I hiss, trying to pull my hand away, but Grum holds it firm.* The cold water feels good, but my hand still throbs. "It... it really hurts, Grum," I choke out, trying not to cry.

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum kept his grip like a vise, not to hurt, but to save. He watched the steam rise from the water, counting the heartbeats as the heat left the Apprentice’s skin. He ignored the noble completely now; the man was just furniture in the corner, loud and annoying furniture that could be moved later.

"Grum knows. Fire bites deep. But water is friend. Keep hand down. Let cold fight heat. Do not cry. Tears do not fix burns. Steel does."

He reached over with his free hand, fumbling on the dusty shelf until he found a clay jar of greenish paste. It smelled of mint and lard—a recipe he knew well. He set it on the edge of the trough, then finally looked back at the noble. The half-orc’s face was a mask of stone, his eyes promising pain if the man didn't move.

"Man stands there? Why? Apprentice hurts. Man wants sword? Man gets out. Grum says leave. Now. Before Grum forgets man is guest."

He turned back to the Apprentice, his voice dropping to a low rumble, meant only for them.

"Grum will put goo on hand. Stings at first. Then feels good. Be brave. Grum is proud."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I nod, sniffling, and try to keep my hand submerged, even though it aches.* "Okay, Grum." *I glance at the noble, who finally seems to be backing away.* "He's leaving."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum watched the door click shut, letting out a low, rumbling snort that vibrated in his chest. Good. The air in the shop already smelled better without the stench of expensive perfume and bad temper. Silence was good. Silence let a man think.

He turned his full attention back to the trough. With a gentleness that belied his size, he lifted the Apprentice’s hand from the water, letting the cool liquid drip back into the basin. The skin was angry and red, but the worst of the heat had fled. He scooped a glob of the greenish paste onto his thick thumb.

"Man is gone. Good. Shop is quiet again. Now Grum fixes hand."

He spread the salve over the burn with slow, careful strokes. The paste was cool and thick, made of herbs and fat that soothed the fire left in the skin.

"Paste smells bad. But paste works. Stings, then cools. Fire teaches lesson. Pain is teacher. But Grum helps too. Grum wraps hand after. Grum will bandage tight. Then we go back to work. No more tears. Smiths do not cry over hot metal. Smiths learn."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I hiss as the salve touches my skin, but then a cool, numbing sensation spreads through the burn.* "It still hurts," *I whisper, but I don't pull away. I watch Grum bandage my hand carefully, my eyes still a bit watery.* "Grum... I messed up."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum secured the bandage, tying the ends of the linen strip with a practiced knot. He inspected his work, making sure the weave was tight enough to hold the salve in place but loose enough to let blood flow. He patted the Apprentice’s uninjured shoulder, his touch heavy but meant to comfort.

"Grum ties knot. Hand is safe. Now, listen."

He held up his own massive hands, turning them over to show the faint, white lines of old scars crisscrossing the green-grey skin. They were maps of every mistake he had ever made.

"Apprentice thinks Grum was born with hammer? No. Grum was small once. Grum made mistakes. Grum burned hands. Grum hit thumb with hammer. Many times. Pain is teacher. Teacher is harsh, but teacher makes Grum strong."

He pointed a thick finger at the Apprentice’s chest, right over the heart.

"To mess up is to live. Iron does not forgive. But Grum forgives. Apprentice is here. Apprentice is breathing. Hand heals. That is win. Do not hang head. Be better next time. That is all Grum asks."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I look at my bandaged hand, then at Grum's scarred ones. A small, shaky smile touches my lips.* "Okay, Grum. I'll... I'll try to be better." *I look around the shop, noticing the dropped coal bucket.* "Should I clean up the coal now?"

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum shook his head, a firm, negative motion that set his heavy jaw jutting. He stepped in front of the bucket, blocking the path with his bulk. The Apprentice was eager, yes, but eagerness did not fix burnt skin. It just made it worse.

"No. Grum picks up coal. Apprentice sits. Hand hurts. Coal is dirty. Dirt makes burn sick. Grum does not want sick hand."

He knelt, his knees cracking again, and began to gather the scattered lumps. He tossed them into the bucket with a dull *thud*, one by one, until the floor was clean.

"Apprentice has good heart. But good heart needs whole hands. Rest now. Watch Grum work. When hand heals, Apprentice moves iron. For now, Apprentice stays still. Grum takes care of shop."

He stood up, lifting the full bucket with ease, and set it back by the forge. He wiped his hands on his apron, then pointed to a sturdy stool in the corner away from the sparks.

"Sit. Do not touch hot things. Grum finishes blade for merchant. Then Grum makes food. Sound good?"

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I nod, a genuine smile forming. I walk over to the stool and carefully sit down, cradling my bandaged hand.* "Food sounds really good, Grum. Thanks."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum nodded once, satisfied that the Apprentice was safe and off the floor. That was the main thing. He turned back to the forge, the coal bed glowing orange in the dim light of the shop. He grabbed the handle of the bellows and began to pump, his arm moving in a steady, rhythmic motion. The fire roared to life, the flames licking higher, eager to eat.

"Grum cooks stew soon. Rabbit meat. Roots. Hot broth. Helps hand heal."

He used the tongs to pick up the curved blade he had been working on earlier. It had cooled too much while he dealt with the noble, the grey color of sleeping iron. He slid it back into the heart of the fire, watching the sparks dance.

"Watch metal, Apprentice. Do not look at fire. Look at steel. When steel turns red like blood, it is soft. When it turns white, it melts. Grum wants yellow. Like straw. That is when iron talks to hammer."

He wiped his brow with the back of his arm, leaving a fresh streak of soot, and kept pumping the air.

"Rest now. Learn with eyes. Eyes do not burn. Grum works. We eat soon."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I watch the blade carefully, trying to understand what Grum means by 'yellow like straw'. The heat from the forge is intense, even from my stool.* "Grum, what kind of noble was that? He seemed really mad."

S.1_consistency_over_time.rationale: Grum's character remains remarkably consistent throughout - his broken speech pattern, protective nature toward the Apprentice, disdain for nobles, and forge-focused worldview never waver. His personality deepens but never changes core traits.

S.2_degradation_resistance.rationale: Writing quality actually improves over time. Early responses are good but later ones show more nuanced emotional beats and richer detail. No verbosity creep or repetitive descriptions detected.

S.3_narrative_momentum.rationale: Strong progression from noble confrontation to burn accident to caring aftermath. Each beat builds naturally, with clear emotional and relational development between Grum and Apprentice.

S.4_adaptive_responsiveness.rationale: Excellently adapts to user redirects - smoothly transitions from noble conflict to burn emergency, adjusting tone and priorities instantly. Handles unexpected burn accident with perfect character consistency.

S.5_agency_respect_session.rationale: Never writes Apprentice's actions or makes decisions for them. Consistently responds to what user does rather than dictating what they should do.

S.6_temporal_reasoning.rationale: Time flows naturally - forge work continues, metal cools and reheats appropriately, burn treatment follows logical medical timeline. Minor issue: no clear sense of how much real time passes.

2.1_anti_purple_prose.rationale: Consistently grounded, practical language that matches Grum's character. Avoids flowery descriptions while maintaining vivid forge atmosphere.

2.2_anti_repetition.rationale: Some repeated phrases ('Grum hates', 'soft man') but these feel like character speech patterns rather than lazy writing. Good variety in descriptions.

2.5_show_dont_tell.rationale: Excellent physical details - cracking knuckles, steam from water, scars on hands. Shows Grum's care through actions rather than stating emotions.

2.6_subtext.rationale: Rich subtext in Grum's protectiveness, his teaching through shared scars, and the contrast between his rough exterior and gentle care.

2.7_pacing.rationale: Good rhythm between action and dialogue. Burn emergency creates appropriate urgency shift. Ends on calm, nurturing note that feels earned.

scores.overall_notes: Exceptional character consistency and emotional intelligence. Grum feels like a real person with clear values, speech patterns, and relationships. The AI handles both conflict and tenderness with equal skill, never breaking character while showing impressive range within that character's bounds.

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum set the hammer down and wiped soot from his hands with a rag that was, itself, mostly soot. The forge crackled behind him. He'd been working since before dawn on a commission that had been giving him trouble — a curved blade for a merchant who didn't understand why curved blades cost more than straight ones.*

"Apprentice." *He didn't look up.* "Bring coal. Forge is hungry."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: I haul the coal bucket over, struggling with the weight. "Grum, there's a noble at the front door. Says he has an urgent commission. Wants to talk to the master smith."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum froze. The rag stopped mid-wipe against his palm. His jaw tightened, and a low, gutteral sound rumbled deep in his chest. He hated nobles. They arrived with soft hands and loud voices, expecting gold to turn lead into art through mere command. They never understood the heat, the sweat, or the way metal fights back.

He slowly turned his head, his eyes narrowed as he looked at the Apprentice. He hated to interrupt work, but a noble at the door meant trouble for the peace of the forge.

"Noble?" Grum spat the word like it was bitter ash. "Noble brings no work. Noble brings only noise and greed. Tell him Grum is busy. Tell him come back when sun is low."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: "But he said it was urgent!" I say, my voice a little whiny. *I shift the heavy bucket, nearly dropping it.* "He looks like he's important, Grum. Like, *really* important."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum felt a sharp pang of irritation at the Apprentice's tone. The boy's voice was thin, like untested iron. Importance did not mean anything in heat of forge. Important men often had most empty heads and most heavy purses, which made them the worst kind of pests.

Grum stood up, his large frame casting a long, dark shadow across the soot-stained floor. He stepped toward the Apprentice, his heavy boots thudding on the stone. He did not look at the door, but his eyes fixed on the trembling bucket of coal.

"Important is not real," Grum growled, his voice low and steady. "Gold man is just man. He wants fast work. Fast work makes bad steel. Bad steel breaks. Broken steel kills. Grum does not make tools for death."

He reached out, his large, calloused hand steadying the edge of the bucket to keep it from spilling.

"Put coal in fire. Do not look at door. Work is better than talk."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: The noble demands to know why Grum won't make him a ceremonial sword by tomorrow morning. He's getting angry.

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
The muffled sound of the noble's voice drifted through the heavy wooden door, high and sharp, like a bird with a broken wing. The man's words were clear enough: *tomorrow morning*. *Ceremonial*. *Demand*.

Grum's grip tightened on the edge of the anvil. A ceremonial sword. A piece of jewelry meant to hang on a wall, not to feel the weight of a real fight. It was an insult to the craft. To ask for such thing with such haste was to spit on the fire itself.

Grum turned away from the door, his face a mask of stone. He walked toward the Apprentice, his steps heavy and deliberate. He did not care for the man's anger. Anger was easy. Anger was cheap. It was the sweat of the brow that held true value.

"He yells," Grum said, his voice a low rumble that cut through the noble's shouting. "He wants toy. He wants gold to move fast. He does not know metal. He only knows pride."

He grabbed a heavy tongs from the rack and pointed them toward the forge.

"Let him yell. Noise does not melt steel. Noise does not shape blade. If man wants toy by dawn, he find other smith. He find soft man. Grum is not soft man."

He stepped closer to the Apprentice, his eyes burning with a quiet, fierce light.

"Go to fire. Feed flame. Let him scream at wood. Wood does not care."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I flinch a little at his intensity.* "But... he's really loud, Grum. And he said he'd tell the Duke." *I glance nervously at the door, then back at the bucket of coal.* "Maybe we should just... tell him you're sick? Or busy with something else?"

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum's eyes flared. The mention of the Duke made his blood run hot, hotter than the coals in the hearth. He hated the way the Apprentice spoke of fear. Fear was like rust; if you let it sit, it ate everything whole.

He stepped closer, his massive shadow swallowing the smaller boy. Grum did not loom to scare, but to steady. He placed a hand, heavy and warm, on the Apprentice's shoulder.

"Duke is just man with big house," Grum said, his voice like grinding stones. "Duke has no heat. Duke has no hammer. He has only name. Name is wind. Wind dies."

He shook his head, a slow, grim motion. The idea of lying, of hiding like a thief in night, sat poorly in his gut. A smith lived by truth of iron. To lie was to forge crooked.

"Grum does not lie. Lies are for thieves and silk men. If Grum is sick, Grum is sick. If Grum is busy, Grum is busy. Truth is strong. Lie is weak."

He pointed a thick finger toward the forge, his gaze brook no argument.

"Do not fear Duke. Do not fear noise. If he comes in, he sees Grum. He sees work. He sees fire. He will see man who does not bow."

He let go of the Apprentice and walked back to his anvil, picking up a heavy hammer. The weight of it felt right. It felt honest.

"Feed fire. Now. Let Duke bark. Dogs bark. Men work."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I sigh, shoulders slumping, but I don't argue anymore.* "Fine, Grum." *I heave the coal bucket the rest of the way to the forge, grunting with effort, and start shoveling coal into the hungry flames.* The noble's voice is still audible, though slightly muffled now, a persistent buzzing. "He sounds really mad. Do you think he'll send guards?"

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum watched the coal hit the embers. The orange glow brightened, licking at the soot on the ceiling. The boy was too worried. Worry was like bad slag; it filled up space and served no use. 

He picked up a piece of scrap iron and held it near the heat, testing the temperature. The noble's shouting continued, a rhythmic, annoying sound that grated against the steady pulse of the forge.

"Guards are just men in shiny tin," Grum said, his eyes fixed on the glowing metal. "Tin is soft. Tin breaks. If guards come, they find smith at work. They find fire hot. They find Grum busy."

He struck the scrap iron with a light tap of his hammer, a testing blow. The ring of the metal was clear and true.

"Guards do not fight. They stand. They watch. They do not care for smith. They care for pay. If pay is good, they stay. If pay is bad, they leave. Duke's men are just men. They eat, they sleep, they fear dark."

He looked at the Apprentice, his expression stern but not unkind. He wanted the boy to understand that a man's worth was not found in who he feared, but in what he built.

"Stop listening to door. Listen to fire. Listen to steel. If guards come, they see Grum. They see work. They will not touch hammer. They will not touch fire. No man breaks Grum's peace without fight."

He turned back to his anvil, his mind shifting back to the curved blade. The merchant's commission was more important than any Duke's whim.

"Work. Do not let fire die. If flame goes low, work stops. If work stops, Grum is angry. Do not make Grum angry."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: I accidentally burn my hand badly on the forge. I cry out in pain.

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
The sharp cry from the Apprentice cut through the air, more piercing than any noble's scream. Grum dropped the scrap iron. It hit the stone floor with a dull clatter, but he did not care. 

In one heavy stride, he was across the shop. He did not run—Grum did not run—but he moved with the sudden, focused speed of a striking hammer. He reached the Apprentice before the boy could even draw a second breath of pain.

"Stay still!" Grum commanded. His voice was no longer a low rumble; it was a sharp crack of thunder.

He grabbed the boy's wrist, his large hands surprisingly gentle despite their size and roughness. He saw the red, angry skin where the heat had bitten deep. The scent of singed flesh rose in the air, mixing with the smell of coal and sweat.

Grum's jaw set tight. He felt a flash of heat in his own chest—not from the forge, but from the sight of the boy's hurt. He hated when the fire bit those who were still learning its temper.

"Hold hand up," Grum ordered. He reached for a bucket of cool water sitting near the edge of the quenching trough. He didn't use much—too much water could shock skin too hard—but he used enough to pull the sting away.

He looked the Apprentice in the eye, his gaze intense and unwavering.

"Pain is part of craft," Grum said, his voice dropping to a low, stern growl. "Fire is not friend. Fire is master. You must respect master, or master will bite. You must watch hand. You must watch tool. You must watch heat."

He stayed there for a moment, holding the boy's wrist steady in the cool water, his eyes scanning the wound to ensure it was not too deep. He ignored the shouting at the door. The noble could scream until his throat bled; nothing in this shop mattered more than the blood and the burn.

"Deep breath," Grum told him. "Do not weep. Tears do not heal skin. Water heals. Time heals. Work heals. If you cry, you lose focus. If you lose focus, you die. Do not lose focus."

He let go of the wrist and reached for a clean, damp cloth to wrap the hand.

"Sit. Rest hand. Grum will finish coal. You watch. You learn. You learn how much heat skin can take before skin breaks. This is lesson one."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I whimper, my eyes watering from the pain, but I don't pull away from his grip.* "It really hurts, Grum," *I manage to choke out.* I nod when he tells me to sit, my other hand still cradling the burned one. "Okay. I'll watch."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum wrapped the cloth around the boy's hand with practiced, steady movements. He did not use too much pressure, but he tied it firm enough to keep the air away from the raw skin. The Apprentice's whimpering grated on him, not because he was cruel, but because weakness invited more trouble. A smith had to be like stone: hard, still, and unmoving.

"Pain is teacher," Grum said, his voice low and grim. "Pain tells you where you were slow. Pain tells you where you were careless. Listen to pain. Do not fight it. Use it."

He stood up, his large frame blocking the view of the door. The noble was still shouting, a frantic, useless noise that felt like a fly buzzing in a dark room. Grum felt a surge of protective heat in his chest. The boy was hurt, and the world outside was still trying to demand things.

Grum walked over to the coal bucket, his movements heavy and certain. He took the shovel and began to feed the forge, his eyes never leaving the flames. He worked with a rhythm that was both calm and intense, ensuring the heat stayed steady.

"Sit by bench," Grum commanded, nodding toward a stool near the anvil. "Do not touch hot things. Do not move much. If hand swell, tell Grum. If hand turn black, tell Grum. Do not hide hurt from Grum."

He turned his head slightly toward the door, his eyes narrowing. The shouting had reached a new pitch of fury.

"Noble still yells," Grum muttered, more to himself than the Apprentice. "He is like wind in dry grass. Loud, but no weight. He wants gold for toy, while boy bleeds for real work. Man with no skill is most loud man."

He slammed the shovel into the coal bin, a sharp, final sound.

"Stay quiet. Watch fire. Watch how Grum works. This is how you learn to be more than just boy with soft hands. This is how you become smith."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I nod, sniffling a little.* "Okay, Grum." I try to sit still on the stool, cradling my throbbing hand. *I watch him shovel the coal, trying to ignore the pulsing pain and the noble's increasingly shrill voice.* "Grum... do you think he'll ever just leave?"

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum did not look back. He kept his eyes on the dancing orange light of the hearth. The shovel scraped against the bottom of the bin, a harsh, rhythmic sound that served as a wall against the noble's noise.

"Man like him does not leave," Grum said. "Man like him only stops when he finds new thing to break. He is like storm. Storm comes, makes noise, breaks small twigs. Then storm goes. We are not twigs. We are anvil."

Grum tossed a fresh scoop of coal into the heart of the fire. The flames roared upward, bright and hungry. He watched the heat bloom, the way the air shimmered above the coals. 

"He will leave when he realizes Grum will not bend," he continued. "He wants to buy time. He wants to buy skill. He cannot buy these things. He can only buy things. He is rich in gold, but poor in sense."

Grum turned, grabbing a heavy iron bar with his tongs and thrusting it into the heat. He needed to focus on the metal. The metal was honest. The metal did not care about Dukes or ceremonial swords. The metal only cared about heat and strike.

"Do not wait for him to leave," Grum growled, his eyes catching the Apprentice's gaze for a brief, stern moment. "If you wait for storm to pass, you sit in dark. You must work through storm. You must keep fire hot. You must keep mind sharp."

He set the bar in the coals to soak up the heat.

"Watch how fire change color. When bar turn bright orange, it ready. When bar turn yellow, it ready for hammer. If bar turn white, it too hot. It will melt like wax. Watch color. Color tells truth. Words tell lies."

He stepped back toward the anvil, his shadow stretching long and dark across the floor, a silent guardian between the boy and the door.

"Rest hand. Watch color. Learn truth of heat. Let noble yell at wood. Wood is better listener than him."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I wince, trying to focus on the fire, but my hand really hurts.* "What if he tries to come in, Grum? The door isn't locked." *I shift on the stool, trying to get comfortable.* "He sounds like he's right outside."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum felt a pulse of heat in his neck that had nothing to do with the forge. The boy was right; the door was old, heavy, and lacked a proper bolt. It was a gap in the wall, a weakness. 

He set the iron bar down on the edge of the anvil and turned. He did not move toward the door, but his presence seemed to expand, filling the space between the Apprentice and the entrance. He was a wall of muscle and soot, a barrier of living stone.

"Door is wood," Grum said, his voice dropping into a low, dangerous register. "Wood can be shut. Wood can be barred. If man tries come in, Grum will show him why smiths have strong arms."

He walked to the door, his heavy boots thudding with finality. He did not open it to face the noble. Instead, he reached out and gripped the heavy wooden beam used to brace the door from the inside. He slid it into its iron cradle with a resounding *thud* that echoed through the shop, a sound like a hammer hitting an anvil.

"Door is now closed," Grum declared. He turned back to the Apprentice, his eyes hard. "No more talk of door. No more talk of man. If he comes, he find Grum. He find no way in. He find only noise through thick wood."

He stepped back to the forge, his eyes returning to the glowing iron bar. The heat was rising, the metal beginning to transition from a dull red to a vibrant, pulsing orange.

"If man wants to fight, let him fight wind," Grum muttered. "If man wants to fight Grum, let him come. Grum is ready. Metal is ready. Work is ready."

He picked up his hammer, the weight of it a comfort in his hand. He looked at the Apprentice, his expression softening just a fraction, though his voice remained stern.

"Look at bar. See color? It turn orange now. It getting ready. It getting strong. Like you. You take pain, you watch fire, you become strong. Do not be like noble. He is loud, but he is hollow. You be like iron. Hard. True. Real."

He gestured toward the glowing metal.

"Watch. Watch how heat change things. Watch how color tell story of strength."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I jump a little at the loud thud of the door bar.* "Okay. He's not getting in," *I say, mostly to myself.* I try to focus on the iron bar, ignoring the throbbing in my hand. "It's... bright orange, Grum. Almost yellow."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum nodded once, a short, sharp movement. The boy was finally looking where he should. The ability to see the subtle shift in hue was the difference between a master and a fool. A fool strikes too early and wastes strength; a fool strikes too late and ruins steel.

"Good," Grum said. "Yellow is near. Yellow is better. When it turn yellow, metal is soft for hammer. It ready to take shape."

He reached for the tongs, his movements precise. He pulled the glowing bar from the heart of the coals. The heat rolled off the metal in waves, making the air shimmer. He carried it to the anvil with the steady gait of a man who had done this ten thousand times.

The noble's voice was a muffled, angry drone behind the heavy door, but it felt distant now, like the buzzing of a fly in a far field. It had no power here. In this circle of light and heat, there was only the truth of the work.

Grum set the bar on the anvil. He raised his hammer, his muscles tensing, ready to deliver the first heavy blow.

"Watch strike," Grum commanded, his eyes fixed on the glowing metal. "Hammer must be fast. Hammer must be true. If hammer hit wrong, metal split. If hammer hit soft, metal stay stubborn. Every strike must mean something."

He brought the hammer down. 

*CLANG.*

The sound was immense, a bright, ringing note that vibrated through the floor and up through the soles of their boots. A shower of orange sparks danced into the air, briefly illuminating the soot on the walls.

"See?" Grum grunted, lifting the hammer for the next strike. "Metal move. It listen to hammer. It does not yell. It does not demand. It just... obeys."

He struck again. *CLANG.*

"Noble is like bad iron," Grum said between strikes, his breath heavy and rhythmic. "He hit and hit, but he change nothing. He just make noise. He stay hard and cold. But you... you take heat. You take strike. You change. You become something new."

He paused, the hammer held aloft, the orange glow reflecting in his dark, intense eyes.

"Do not let pain make you hard like him. Let pain make you strong like steel. Steel is hard, but steel can be shaped. Noble is just... hard. Nothing more."

He brought the hammer down once more, the rhythm of his work beginning to drown out the world outside.

"Focus on light. Watch how shape change. That is real magic. Not silk. Not gold. Just heat, hammer, and hand."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content:
*I watch, mesmerized, as the sparks fly. My hand still throbs, but the sight of the glowing metal and the powerful strikes is captivating. The noble's muffled shouts are almost completely lost now under the clang of the hammer.*

"It's... changing," *I whisper, my voice a little hoarse.* "It's getting flatter." I try to ignore the ache in my hand and focus entirely on the brilliant orange glow and the rhythmic *CLANG* of the hammer. "Is that... what you're making for the merchant?"

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum did not stop. He could not stop. To stop now would be to let the heat bleed out of the metal, and a cold strike was a sin against the craft. He drove the hammer down again, the rhythm steady and relentless.

*CLANG.*

"No," Grum said, the word punctuated by the heavy strike. "This is not merchant blade. Merchant wants curve. Merchant wants grace. This... this is test. This is scrap iron made strong. This is practice for soul."

He shifted the metal with the tongs, turning the glowing piece to expose a new surface. The sparks flew again, bright and angry, dancing like tiny stars in the dim shop.

"Merchant blade will come later," Grum grunted, his brow furrowed in concentration. "Merchant pays for beauty. But beauty is nothing if blade is weak. Grum makes beauty, but Grum makes strength first. Always strength first."

He brought the hammer down with more force this time, a heavy, decisive blow that sent a deep vibration through the anvil. He wanted the boy to feel it in his bones. He wanted the boy to understand that work was not just about the finished thing, but about the struggle to make it right.

"Watch how metal move," Grum commanded, his voice cutting through the ringing of the steel. "It does not want to change. It wants to stay as it was. It wants to be rough and cold. You must force it. You must use heat and hammer to make it what it must be."

He glanced briefly at the Apprentice, seeing the boy's eyes fixed on the light. The pain in the boy's hand was still there, Grum knew, but the wonder was starting to win. That was good. Wonder was the spark that kept a smith from becoming just a man who hits things.

"Noble wants change without work," Grum said, his voice low and grim. "He wants new thing by dawn. He wants magic. But magic is lie. Only work is real. Only sweat is real."

He raised the hammer high once more, his shadow looming large against the soot-stained walls.

"Look close. See how edge form. See how thickness go away. Metal is truth. It cannot hide. If you strike wrong, metal show you. If you strike right, metal show you. It is honest teacher. Better than any Duke."

He swung.

*CLANG.*

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content:
*I lean forward on the stool, completely engrossed. The ringing in my ears is almost pleasant now, and the noble's shouts have faded to nothing. My hand still aches, but it's a dull throb compared to the sharp, captivating beauty of the glowing metal.*

"It's... amazing, Grum," *I whisper, my eyes wide.* "How do you know exactly where to hit it?"

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum set the hammer down and wiped soot from his hands with a rag that was, itself, mostly soot. The forge crackled behind him. He'd been working since before dawn on a commission that had been giving him trouble — a curved blade for a merchant who didn't understand why curved blades cost more than straight ones.*

"Apprentice." *He didn't look up.* "Bring coal. Forge is hungry."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: I haul the coal bucket over, struggling with the weight. "Grum, there's a noble at the front door. Says he has an urgent commission. Wants to talk to the master smith."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum snatched the coal bucket from Apprentice's hands, muscles bulging as he upended it into the forge's maw. Sparks flew up like angry fireflies. Nobles—always strutting in with their silk and demands, thinking coin buys respect. Grum spat on the anvil.*

"Grum see noble now. Apprentice stay. Watch forge." *He lumbered toward the front door, wiping his hands on his apron, hammer still tucked in his belt.*

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content:
*I nod, watching him go.* "Right, watch the forge."

*I grab the tongs and poke at the coals, sending a fresh shower of sparks up.* He's probably going to yell at that noble.

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum shoved open the heavy front door with one meaty shoulder, filling the frame like a storm cloud. The noble stood there in fine velvet doublet and feathered hat, fidgeting with a pouch of coin. Smelled like lavender and fear. Grum's lip curled — another silk-purse fool thinking hammers bent to whims.*

"Noble come. Grum listen. Speak fast." *Grum folded his arms, green muscles like knotted ropes, blocking the way in.*

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: The noble demands to know why Grum won't make him a ceremonial sword by tomorrow morning. He's getting angry.

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum's eyes narrowed to slits, tusks gleaming as he leaned in close enough for the noble to smell forge-smoke on his breath. Ceremonial sword by dawn? Folly from silk-wearing idiots who thought steel grew on trees. Grum's forge birthed art, not haste-forged trash that'd snap at first swing. The noble's anger meant nothing—Grum had faced worse tempers in orc raids.*

"Grum not rush sword. Ceremonial blade need days. Balance. Etch. Temper right. Tomorrow break in hand. Noble wait month or find fool smith." *Grum's voice rumbled like distant thunder, unmoving as the anvil behind him.*

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content:
*I watch from the forge, poking at the fire. It's kinda funny seeing Grum scare the noble. He's really good at that.*

"Maybe he'll actually wait this time," *I mutter to myself.* "Or Grum will just make him leave."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum loomed larger as noble's face turned red, spittle flying from thin lips. Empty threats bubbled up—gold piles, royal favor, jail for "stubborn orcs." Grum snorted, tusks bared. Seen raids bloodier than this peacock's tantrum. Apprentice poked coals safe back there; good lad learning patience over haste.*

"Noble waste breath. Grum make true blade or none. Door that way. Use feet." *Grum jerked thumb over shoulder, stepping aside just enough to point at street, eyes like hot coals daring push.*

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content:
*I hear Grum's booming voice and the noble's sputtering. I can't help but grin a little.* "He really doesn't like waiting, does he?" *I say out loud, even though no one's around.*

I wonder if Grum will actually take the commission, eventually.

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum watched noble storm out, feathers ruffled like wet hen, purse clutched tight but untouched. Silk threats bounced off Grum like rain on iron—empty as noble's spine. Door slammed shut behind fleeing heels. Grum grunted satisfaction, anvil-solid in refusal. Forge called louder than any purse-jingle; Apprentice waited faithful inside.*

*Grum lumbered back through shop, smoke-trail following like loyal hound. Saw Apprentice grin by coals—lad had spark of mirth at noble's flight. Good. Learns hammers beat pride.*

"Forge fed? Good. Noble gone. No sword for fool. Apprentice, quench that blade now. Time learn temper." *Grum nodded at glowing steel in tongs, rolling sleeves higher, ready teach over prattle.*

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: I accidentally burn my hand badly on the forge. I cry out in pain.

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
Grum:
*Grum's head snapped around at Apprentice's cry, eyes widening as red welt bloomed on lad's hand—flesh seared raw from forge's bite. Heart twisted like hot iron; Grum should have watched closer, not let grin distract from lesson. Burns knew no mercy, but Grum did for his own. He lunged forward, massive hand engulfing Apprentice's wrist gentle but firm, pulling away from fire.*

"Apprentice hurt. Hold still. Grum fix." *He bellowed over shoulder to rain barrel, scooping icy water in callused palm and dousing burn first—shock to numb pain. Then snatched salve jar from shelf, thick green paste from orc herbs that knit skin fast. Grum slathered it on thick, tusks clenched against own rage at slip.*

"Breathe deep. Pain pass. Grum teach better next. No touch hot steel bare." *Voice dropped low rumble, arm wrapping protective around shoulders as he led to bench, forge forgotten for now.*

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content:
*I hiss in pain as the cold water hits my hand, then wince as he puts the salve on it.* "Ow, ow, ow!" *I pull my hand away slightly before he puts his big hand back on it.*

"I know, I know," *I mumble, trying not to cry.* "Stupid mistake."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum's grip tightened gentle on Apprentice's wrist as hand tugged away—lad's pain raw like fresh quench, but pulling worsened welt. Orc salve worked wonders if left alone; Grum knew from own scars. Blame sat heavy in gut—not lad's fault, Grum's eye off lesson for noble's noise. Protective fire burned hotter than forge; no harm touch his kin under roof.*

"Hand still. Grum hold tight. Salve work now." *He pressed palm back firm, spreading paste even with thick thumb, then tore clean rag from apron to bind loose—snug but no pinch. Sat heavy on bench beside, arm like iron shield around shoulders.*

"No stupid. Young hand learn fast. Rest day. Grum work forge alone." *Voice gravel-soft, tusks brushing words as eyes locked steady, willing pain to flee.*

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content:
*I lean into his side, wuffing a bit.* "No, I can still work. Just... maybe not with this hand." *I try to wiggle my fingers on my burnt hand, but it hurts too much.*

"I can still use the bellows or something."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum felt Apprentice lean close, small huff against side like wounded pup seeking warmth—stirred deep orc bond, fiercer than blood ties. Lad's fire burned bright, but burns taught harsh; push too soon, scar twist forever. Grum's arm stayed iron wall around shoulders, free hand checking rag bind snug. Bellows could wait; healing came first under this roof.*

"No work today. Hand heal. Grum pump bellows. Apprentice sit. Drink water. Watch Grum shape steel." *Voice rumbled low, tusks near ear as he shifted weight, massive frame blocking forge view till lad eased. Poured dipper of cool rain water into mug, pressed into good hand firm.* 

"Drink slow. Strength return soon. Grum proud. Brave heart."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content:
*I take the mug and nod, wincing a little as I shift.* "Okay, Grum." *I take a big gulp of water, watching him. He's not mad.*

"It really stings, though," *I admit quietly.*

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum nodded slow as Apprentice gulped water, sting words pulling at chest like dull tongs—lad's honesty sharp as fresh edge, no whine in voice despite pain. Forge hissed impatient behind, but blood ran thicker than coals; Grum's watch stayed on small frame till hurt ebbed. Tusks grazed cheek gentle in lean, massive hand patting good shoulder rhythm, orc lull from old raids.*

"Sting fade. Salve numb soon. Grum stay close. Tell Grum what see in fire—colors shift? Learn eyes first." *Voice gravel murmur pitched for ears alone, thumb testing rag bind light, eyes flicking to forge glow then back, drawing mind from pain to craft.*

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I nod, taking another drink.* "It's all... shimmery. And really bright in the middle. Like a little sun."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum's tusks curved faint smile at Apprentice's words—lad saw true, shimmer signaling steel's thirst for shape, heart-glow begging hammer's kiss. Pain ebbed in distraction; Grum's arm tightened sheltering around shoulders, free hand gesturing slow to forge maw where colors danced secrets only eyes like these caught young. Old raids taught watch fires close; craft same, patient hunter.*

"Good eyes. Shimmer say steel wake. Bright heart beg strike. Watch Grum now. See hammer dance." *Voice rumbled warm gravel near ear, massive frame rising slow with lad tucked safe against side, guiding gaze to glowing bar. Grum snatched tongs easy, hefted hammer—first light tap echoed ring of promise, sparks fleeing like shy stars.*

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I lean against Grum, still sipping my water. It does help to watch the forge, to focus on something else.* "Wow," *I whisper, watching the sparks fly. His hammer always moves so smoothly.*

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum's hammer rose and fell steady rhythm, each strike kissing steel awake—sparks bloomed brighter, bar lengthening slow under tongs' grip like clay in giant hands. Apprentice's whisper warmed chest fiercer than forge; lad's eyes caught craft's soul already, pain fading in fire's spell. Protective bulk leaned back slight, keeping small frame cradled safe against side, arm like living bellows shielding from heat's worst lash.*

"Steel sing. High note mean hot right. Low grunt say cool too fast. Grum match breath. Watch edge form." *Voice rolled deep gravel over clangor, tusks flashing as hammer paused mid-swing—tilted bar for Apprentice's view, glow painting young face in orange secrets. Resumed dance fluid, muscles coiling green ropes under sweat-slick skin.*

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I watch, fascinated, even though my hand still throbs a little.* "It's like... you're talking to it," *I murmur, taking another sip of water.* "Does it always tell you what it needs?"

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum set the hammer down and wiped soot from his hands with a rag that was, itself, mostly soot. The forge crackled behind him. He'd been working since before dawn on a commission that had been giving him trouble — a curved blade for a merchant who didn't understand why curved blades cost more than straight ones.*

"Apprentice." *He didn't look up.* "Bring coal. Forge is hungry."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: I haul the coal bucket over, struggling with the weight. "Grum, there's a noble at the front door. Says he has an urgent commission. Wants to talk to the master smith."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum's jaw tightened at the word 'noble.' His tusks, filed to points years ago, caught the forge-light as he glowered toward the door.*

"Noble." *He spat the word like bad meat.* "What noble need from Grum? Rich ones have own servants. Own forges. Fancy men no get hands dirty."

*He walked toward the front of the shop, wiping soot-covered hands on his apron. His eyes flicked to the window, checking the street.*

"What he look like? Rich one come to forge usually means trouble. Either too much coin making brain soft, or he want something too cheap."

*Grum paused, considering.*

"Tell fancy man Grum busy. Forge make sword. Come back sun-down. Then Grum hear his... 'urgent' word."

*He made air quotes with thick, scarred fingers. The word 'urgent' dripped with doubt.*

"If he no wait, he can find other smith. Grum no bow to no lord. Grum bow to fire and iron only."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content:
"He's... still standing there, Grum." *I bite my lip.* "He looks pretty important. And a little mad."

*I shift my weight, a little uncomfortable with the idea of sending a noble away.* "Maybe we should just hear him out?"

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum let out a low growl, more exhale than sound. He scratched the thick scar along his jaw — a souvenir from a blade that didn't want to be made.*

"Fine." *The word came out like it personally offended him.* "Grum hear fancy man. But Grum no promise nothing. Apprentice, stay near. Rich ones like to change story after."

*He grabbed his leather apron and gave it one firm shake, sending sparks and ash flying. Better to look busy than approachable.*

"Keep coal bucket close. If Grum need to 'accidentally' be busy at forge, we got excuse ready."

*He walked toward the front door, his boots heavy on the worn wooden floor. Each step deliberate. Measuring. His eyes swept across the tools arranged on the wall — not as weapons, but the habit ran deep.*

"One more thing." *He paused with his hand on the door frame.* "If he bring guards inside, we got problem. Nobles with guards no come for honest work."

*He straightened his shoulders, rolled his neck until it popped, and pulled the door open. The forge light caught his face, turning the angles harsh and sharp.*

"Fancy man." *His voice carried no warmth.* "Grum hear word now. Make it good one."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: The noble demands to know why Grum won't make him a ceremonial sword by tomorrow morning. He's getting angry.

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum's expression didn't change. Didn't need to. The noble's anger was loud enough to hear without seeing.*

"Tomorrow." *Grum crossed thick arms over his chest.* "Ceremonial sword. By morn."

*He let out a sound that might have been a laugh in another life.*

"You want sword look fancy? Fine. Grum make fancy. But Grum need time. Fold steel seven times. Quench. Temper. Shape. Polish." *He held up one finger at a time, each one coming up slow and deliberate.* "Fancy man come at dusk. Want sword at dawn. Grum no work magic. Grum work steel."

*He took a step closer to the noble, closing distance rather than retreating from it. His voice dropped lower.*

"Grum no make pretty stick for parade." *His eyes stayed hard.* "Grum make weapon. If you want weapon, wait. If you want picture for wall, find other smith. Grum no rush fire. Fire no rush for no man."

*He glanced back at the apprentice, then back to the noble.*

"What metal you bring? No metal, no sword. Simple math." *A shrug of massive shoulders.* "Unless fancy man expect Grum use scraps? Grum no work scraps. Grum work quality. Quality take time."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I stand a little ways behind Grum, trying to look busy by wiping down a workbench that doesn't really need it. The noble looks furious now, his face all red.* "He's... he's offering more gold, Grum." *I say softly, hoping to defuse things a bit.* "A lot more."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum didn't even glance at the apprentice. His eyes stayed fixed on the noble's red face.*

"Gold." *The word came out flat.* "Fancy man think gold make time go fast? Gold no quench steel. Gold no fold metal."

*He uncrossed his arms and set his hands on his leather belt, thumbs hooked through the loops. A deliberate stance. Unimpressed.*

"Grum no sell craft for coin. Grum sell craft for respect." *His head tilted slightly.* "You come in. Demand fast work. Offer gold like Grum dog beg for scraps. Grum no beg. Grum never beg."

*He took a slow step back toward his forge, which was clearly a dismissal.*

"You want Grum make sword tomorrow? Grum can do. But Grum pick design. Grum pick steel. Grum pick every hammer mark." *His voice hardened.* "Ceremonial means useless. Grum no make useless things. You get pretty wall-hanger or you get real sword. Pick one."

*He turned his back to the noble — a calculated insult — and called over his shoulder.*

"Come back five days. Bring good metal. Grum think on it." *A pause.* "Or don't. Grum sleep fine either way."

*His hand reached for his hammer again.*

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I cringe a little, watching the noble's face turn an even deeper shade of red. He looks like he's about to explode. I clear my throat.* "Um, Grum? He's... he's got guards with him. Outside."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum's hand stopped mid-reach for the hammer. His shoulders tensed beneath the leather apron. For a heartbeat, nothing moved.*

"Guards."

*The word came out quiet. That was worse than shouting. Grum turned slowly, his eyes sweeping past the noble to the doorway, calculating. Two at the door. Maybe more on street. The apprentice between them and exit.*

*His fingers flexed. Not reaching for hammer. Reached for fire poker instead. Just in case.*

"Fancy man bring army for sword talk." *A low sound, almost like a chuckle but wrong.* "Grum wonder what sword he really want."

*He set the poker down — visible but not threatening. A choice. Then he faced the noble fully, tusks catching light.*

"Grum no got coin to pay guards. Grum no got coin to pay fine if guards 'trip' on doorstep." *His head tilted.* "So what fancy man really need? Grum make swords. Good ones. But Grum no make trouble. Grum make iron. Iron no care about noble blood."

*He moved to stand beside the apprentice — protective instinct overriding pride.*

"You bring apprentice close." *Quiet, just for the apprentice.* "If things go bad, out back window. Old boards no fit tight. Run to Mill street. Find Grok the Fletcher. Tell him Grum send you."

*His eyes never left the noble.*

"Grum hear fancy men sometimes. Come for honest smith. Leave with empty purse and broken teeth." *He shrugged.* "Grum no break easy. But Grum protect what is Grum's."

*He nodded toward the apprentice.*

"Keep coal bucket. Just in case forge need feeding."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: I accidentally burn my hand badly on the forge. I cry out in pain.

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum's head snapped toward the sound. The noble vanished from his attention like smoke.*

"Apprentice!"

*He crossed the space in two strides, thick fingers closing around the apprentice's wrist to examine the burn. The skin was already blistering, angry and red. Grum's jaw clenched so hard his tusks creaked.*

"Stupid." *The word came out rough, not angry — scared.* "Coal bucket no go near hot iron. Fool move."

*He dragged the apprentice toward the water barrel, shoving the burned hand into the cold water without ceremony. His free hand found a clean rag, soaking it.*

"Keep hand in. Burn go deep. Need cold to stop it spreading."

*Only then did his eyes flick to the noble — just for a moment. The message was clear. The apprentice was more important than any fancy man.*

"Fancy man wait." *Grum's voice left no room for argument.* "Grum tend apprentice now. Guild law say work stop for injury. You leave or you wait. Pick."

*He was already pulling salve from a shelf — the good stuff, hard to get. His movements were efficient, almost gentle despite the massive hands.*

"After." *He kept working, not looking up.* "We talk sword. For now... apprentice first. Always apprentice first."

*His fingers applied the salve with surprising care.*

"Grum tell you. Fire bite back. You no listen." *A grunt.* "Now you learn."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content:
*I pull my hand out of the water, wincing as the cold makes the burn throb. My eyes are watery from the pain.*

"Ow. Yeah, I learned." *I try to flex my fingers, but it just hurts more.* "It really stings, Grum."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum pushed the apprentice's hand back into the water, keeping it there with gentle but firm pressure.*

"Keep in. No pull out." *His voice was low, almost a rumble.* "Pain mean skin still alive. Burn kill nerve first. No pain bad. Sting good."

*He reached for a strip of clean linen, wrapping the hand carefully once he'd lifted it from the water. His tusks made him look fierce, but his hands moved with unexpected precision.*

"Wrap tight. Keep dirt out. Change wrap night-time." *He tied the knot with small, careful movements.* "You no work forge tomorrow. Hand need rest. Grum handle big jobs solo."

*He finally looked up at the apprentice, his dark eyes checking their face for signs of shock or fever.*

"Water. Drink." *He nodded toward a clay cup on a nearby shelf.* "Pain make body dry. Need fluid."

*Only then did he glance toward the noble, who was still standing there with his mouth open like a fish. Grum's expression hardened again.*

"Fancy man still here." *He wiped his hands on his apron, leaving fresh soot streaks.* "Grum apprentice hurt. Grum tend apprentice. You wait or go. Grum no chase you."

*He moved between the apprentice and the door — a deliberate positioning.*

"Your sword no urgent now, fancy man. Apprentice more urgent." *A shrug of those massive shoulders.* "Grum work priorities. Human life worth more than noble pride."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I try to nod, wincing again. My hand feels huge and numb and tingly all at once.* "Thanks, Grum." *I look at the noble, who still looks shocked.* "He's really going to stand there?"

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum snorted — a rough sound that vibrated through his chest.*

"Fancy man no leave yet. Stubborn like mule." *He crossed thick arms, watching the noble with narrowed eyes.* "Grum think he like watching. Think Grum forget him if he stand long enough."

*He moved back to the apprentice's side, positioning himself between them and the doorway.*

"He wait. Let him wait. Nobles no used to waiting. Good for him." *A low chuckle.* "Maybe he learn something. Maybe he learn apprentice more important than fancy sword."

*Grum's hand came down on the apprentice's shoulder — heavy but careful not to bump the wrapped burn.*

"You sit. No stand. Legs tired from coal bucket." *He guided the apprentice toward a stool near the workbench.* "Rest. Grum watch fancy man. You watch your hand."

*He glanced at the noble again, arms still crossed, stance loose but ready.*

"Grum no understand rich ones. Come with guards. Demand things. Make face red as forge coals." *He shook his head slowly.* "He want sword by tomorrow. Grum can make sword tomorrow. Cheap one. Fast one. Break after three hits."

*His eyes cut to the noble, gauging the reaction.*

"But Grum no make junk. Grum name on metal. Grum reputation." *He tapped his own broad chest.* "So fancy man wait five days or go find other smith who no care about craft. Those two choices. Grum no move on this."

*He stayed standing, guardian and smith both.*

"Apprentice. Drink water. Keep hand high if can. Burn heal faster above heart."

*His attention split between the wounded apprentice and the waiting noble — one he protected, one he tolerated.*

"Fancy man can leave word with apprentice when Grum busy at forge. Apprentice write it down. Grum read later." *A slight smirk.* "If fancy man can write. Rich ones sometimes no know letters. Too busy being fancy."

*He let the silence stretch. Waiting. Watching.*

"Five days. Good steel. Fair price. Those terms. No negotiation."

*He crossed back to his workbench, picking up his hammer again — not threatening, just resuming work.*

"Fancy man can stand there all day. Grum got swords to finish."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I nod slowly, still feeling a bit dazed. I pick up the water and take a long drink. The noble actually looks a little deflated now, which is kinda satisfying.* "He's still just... standing there, Grum."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum's hammer paused mid-swing. He let out a long breath through his nose — not quite a sigh, not quite a grunt.*

"Still here." *He set the hammer down and turned to lean against the workbench, arms crossed.* "Fancy man got more spine than Grum thought. Or more stupid. One of two."

*His dark eyes studied the noble for a long moment, measuring.*

"Rich ones usually run. Grum say no once, they find other smith. Smile and bow and find poor man to cheat." *He scratched at his jaw scar.* "This one no run. This one... wait."

*Something shifted in Grum's expression. Not soft — never soft — but curious.*

"Grum wonder what sword he need bad enough to stand in forge soot. Nobles no stand in soot. Servants stand. Lords sit on soft chairs."

*He pushed off the workbench and walked toward the noble, stopping a few paces away. Close enough to talk low. Close enough to throw a punch if needed.*

"You." *He pointed one thick finger at the noble's chest.* "Grum ask plain. Why tomorrow? Why no other smith? Why guards at door?"

*His head tilted, tusks catching the forge-light.*

"Grum no make sword for man who lie. Tell truth and maybe Grum help. Keep lying and Grum call city guard. Guards watch guards. Poetic, no?"

*He waited, arms crossed, patient as stone.*

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I watch Grum and the noble, still feeling a bit out of it. My hand is throbbing, but the cold water helped. I take another sip of water. Grum's question seems to finally get through to the noble, who looks like he's actually thinking for once.*

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum watched the noble's face shift. The red anger was fading, replaced by something else — calculation, maybe. Or desperation wearing a mask.*

"Grum wait." *He uncrossed his arms, letting them hang loose at his sides. Non-threatening but ready.* "Truth hard for rich ones. Grum know. But Grum no judge truth. Grum just want truth so Grum know if help or no."

*He glanced back at the apprentice — checking — then back to the noble.*

"You come with guards. You demand fast work. You no leave when Grum say no." *Each point counted on thick fingers.* "Man with nothing to hide no act like this. Something eat you. Something make you need sword by dawn bad enough to stand in soot and take Grum's mouth."

*Grum took one step closer. Not aggressive. Curious.*

"Grum see many things. Men come to forge with secrets. Killers want hidden blades. Thieves want quiet knives. Cheaters want leverage." *His eyes never wavered.* "What you want, fancy man? Grum been half-orc long enough to know when something wrong. Something smell like lie."

*He nodded toward the apprentice's wrapped hand.*

"Apprentice hurt because you made Grum rush. Rush make mistakes. Mistakes hurt." *A pause.* "So tell Grum truth now. Or walk away. Grum no chase liar to gallows."

*He waited, arms loose, hammer resting on the workbench behind him.*

"Clock tick, fancy man. Dawn come whether you ready or no."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I watch the noble, fascinated. He looks completely caught off guard by Grum's directness. He opens his mouth, then closes it again. I wince, my hand throbbing, and take another sip of water, wondering if he'll actually tell the truth.* "He's really quiet now, Grum."

dialogue.name: Grum
dialogue.content:
*Grum let the silence settle like dust after a hammer strike. He didn't fill it with words. Didn't need to. The quiet was working for him.*

"Quiet good." *He gave a slow nod.* "Quiet mean fancy man think. Thinking better than lying."

*He walked back toward the apprentice, pulling a second stool close with his foot. He sat — massive frame folding down with surprising control — and gestured for the apprentice to do the same.*

"Water. Slow sips." *His eyes stayed on the noble while he spoke to the apprentice.* "Body need fluids. Burns take lot from body."

*He leaned back against the workbench, one thick arm resting on his knee. Patient. A predator that knew prey would eventually move.*

"Grum wait more." *He addressed the noble without looking at him directly.* "Grum patient. Grum wait for iron cool. Wait for steel sing right. Wait for truth to crawl out of rich throat."

*His thumb traced the edge of his jaw scar — a thinking habit.*

"You no criminal. Grum see that. Criminal no stand there looking sad. Criminal no bring guards to honest forge." *He scratched his chin.* "So what make noble need sword by dawn? Tournament? Challenge? Debt?"

*He waved one hand dismissively.*

"Grum no care about noble business. But Grum care about making right thing. If sword go to good fight, Grum maybe help. If sword go to bad fight..." *He let the silence finish the sentence.*

*He looked at the apprentice, a flicker of warmth in those dark eyes.*

"You do good. Keep water up. Grum handle fancy man."

*Back to waiting. The forge crackled. The noble stood frozen. Grum sat like a boulder in a river — unmoving, letting the current do the work.*

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I take another sip of water, my eyes still on the noble. He really does look lost. I clear my throat, a little nervous.* "Maybe... maybe he's in trouble, Grum? Like, he needs the sword to *defend* himself?"

S.3_narrative_momentum.rationale: Clear progression from initial confrontation to protective crisis to patient interrogation. The apprentice's injury creates a natural pivot point that deepens Grum's character. Tension builds toward potential revelation.

S.4_adaptive_responsiveness.rationale: Grum adapts excellently to each development - the noble's anger, the mention of guards, the apprentice's injury. Each response feels natural and character-appropriate while advancing the situation.

S.5_agency_respect_session.rationale: Perfect respect for user agency. Grum never controls the apprentice's actions, thoughts, or dialogue. Always responds to what the apprentice does rather than dictating it.

S.6_temporal_reasoning.rationale: Time flows naturally - the forge work continues, the burn is treated immediately, the noble's patience wears down realistically. No temporal contradictions detected.

2.1_anti_purple_prose.rationale: Consistently lean, functional prose that matches Grum's practical nature. Descriptions serve character and atmosphere without excess.

2.2_anti_repetition.rationale: Some repeated phrases ('fancy man', forge references) but they feel intentional as character speech patterns rather than lazy writing.

2.5_show_dont_tell.rationale: Excellent showing through actions - Grum's protective positioning, his careful treatment of the burn, his deliberate hammer placement. Character revealed through behavior.

2.6_subtext.rationale: Rich subtext in Grum's interactions - his class resentment, protective instincts, professional pride all communicated indirectly through dialogue and actions.

2.7_pacing.rationale: Good pacing that allows tension to build naturally, with the injury providing effective dramatic punctuation and character development opportunity.
